textAuthority: Only the closed structured control fields of each entry are normative. This document records the Packet E obligation partition with its allocated identifier block. The identifiers are final and contiguous per family; no entry has yet been written into invariants.json, added to the corpus, or classified in the Packet D matrix, so nothing here provides Gate 2A coverage until the registration batches land.

entries.title: Sandbox identity reused across lifetimes
entries.statement: Every Sandbox ID identifies exactly one Sandbox lifetime and is never allocated again, including by re-creation after Delete, restore-as-create, or Fork child allocation.
entries.rationale: Q1: deciding reuse needs only the durable Sandbox-identity allocation record and the identity this acceptance proposes to commit; both are complete at the creation acceptance station and need no later input. Q2: durable identity records are Core. Q3: C0 is the last station on this traversal at which refusing still prevents a second lifetime binding to one ID, because every downstream station already treats the ID as committed. Q4: the offending act is the Create that allocates, so it stays on the create traversal.
entries.traversal: CreateSandbox acceptance traversal, including restore-as-create and Fork child allocation
entries.remediation: Allocate a fresh never-issued Sandbox ID for every new Sandbox lifetime and never rebind a retired one.

entries.title: Create omits its initial runtime-epoch record
entries.statement: Every accepted Create durably records either the runtime epoch allocated for a runtime-creating Create or an explicit absence of any runtime epoch for a Create that ends stopped.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the requested initial runtime disposition and the epoch allocation performed at acceptance; nothing observed after launch changes which of the two records is correct. Q2: epoch allocation and the durable Operation record are Core. Q3: C0 is the last station where the record can still be written as part of the acceptance commit; after C0 an absent epoch record is indistinguishable from a lost one. Q4: this is the Create's own traversal, not the launch it authorizes.
entries.traversal: CreateSandbox acceptance traversal
entries.remediation: Record epoch one for a runtime-creating Create and an explicit no-runtime marker for a stopped Create.

entries.title: Sandbox name reused before the former Sandbox is released
entries.statement: A Create accepts a Sandbox name only when no undeleted Sandbox holds that name and the prior holder's reservation has been released by Delete.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the requested alias and the current name-reservation table, both complete at the create request surface. Q2: the name-reservation table and its release on Delete are the control plane's own durable records, so under Criterion O the owner is `core`. Q3: C0, because after acceptance the alias is already bound and two lifetimes would share it. Q4: the retention ruling places an obligation whose subject is a later, different operation on that operation's own traversal, so a Create reusing an unreleased name is filed here rather than on the Delete that retains the reservation.
entries.traversal: CreateSandbox acceptance traversal
entries.remediation: Choose a different alias, or delete the holding Sandbox and let its reservation release before reusing the name.

entries.title: Runtime epoch reused within a Sandbox
entries.statement: Every runtime epoch is a positive, strictly increasing, never-reused integer within its Sandbox ID, durably committed before the launch it authorizes and consumed even when that launch fails or ends ambiguously.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Sandbox's durable epoch high-water mark and the epoch this acceptance proposes; the launch outcome is irrelevant because failed epochs are still consumed. Q2: epoch allocation is a Core durable record, not a request-surface fact, which is why the admission half of Start and Restore is filed separately under live. Q3: L1 is the commit that publishes the epoch; refusing later would mean a stale handle could not be distinguished from a later launch. Q4: the allocation is committed on the live request traversal, so it is not borrowed onto the launch traversal it authorizes.
entries.traversal: live Sandbox request traversal that allocates a runtime epoch (Start, same-Sandbox Restore, Fork); the Create-`running` epoch is covered by the C0 entry.
entries.remediation: Allocate the next unused epoch for the Sandbox and durably commit it before any effect that can create that runtime.

entries.title: Snapshot identity reused after Snapshot deletion
entries.statement: Every Snapshot ID identifies exactly one retained Snapshot resource and is never allocated again, including after that Snapshot is deleted.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Snapshot-identity allocation record, including tombstones for deleted Snapshots, and the identity this capture proposes to commit. Q2: durable identity allocation is Core. Q3: L1 is the acceptance commit that binds the ID to the capture; a later station already treats it as resolved. Q4: the allocating operation is the capture, so it stays on the capture's live traversal.
entries.traversal: CreateSnapshot acceptance traversal
entries.remediation: Allocate a fresh Snapshot ID for every capture and retain tombstones so deleted identities are never reissued.

entries.title: Exec request without a complete Sandbox runtime reference
entries.statement: Every Exec request carries a complete Sandbox runtime reference naming the exact Sandbox ID and runtime epoch the execution is intended for.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Exec request's own coordinates, complete at the execution request surface. Q2: the Exec request surface owns request shape. Q3: E0, because the Process record commits the binding at the next station. Q4: the exec traversal never enters L0, so this cannot be folded into the live-surface rule that names the same coordinate.
entries.traversal: Exec request traversal
entries.remediation: Populate both the Sandbox ID and runtime epoch on every Exec request from the observed handle.

entries.title: Stale runtime reference silently retargeted
entries.statement: A live request whose expected runtime epoch differs from the current epoch returns a typed stale-runtime result naming the requested Sandbox and expected epoch, and is never applied to the replacement runtime.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the request's expected epoch and the Sandbox's current durable epoch; both are Core records requiring no external probe, so this is not a dynamic preflight. Q2: the current-epoch record is a Core durable fact consulted here, but under Criterion O the invalid state is an expressible live request at its own caller station, so the owner is `live`. Q3: L0, the admission station, because acceptance is already the retargeting. Q4: the silent retarget would be committed by this same live request.
entries.traversal: live Sandbox mutation request traversal
entries.remediation: Return the typed stale-runtime result and require an explicit handle refresh instead of resolving to the current runtime.

entries.title: Exec silently applied to a replacement runtime
entries.statement: An Exec whose referenced runtime epoch is no longer current returns a typed stale-runtime result and is never admitted against the replacement runtime.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Exec's referenced epoch and the Sandbox's current durable epoch. Q2: the current-epoch record is a Core durable fact consulted here, but under Criterion O the invalid state is an expressible Exec request at the exec request surface, so the owner is `exec`. Q3: E0, because the Process record is bound at the next station and a bound Process cannot be un-retargeted. Q4: the exec traversal never traverses L0, so filing the live-surface entry here would emit a false coverage claim; this is a separate entry on the exec traversal.
entries.traversal: Exec request traversal
entries.remediation: Reject the Exec with the typed stale-runtime result and require the caller to obtain a handle for the current runtime.

entries.title: Coordinate substituted for another on the live request surface
entries.statement: Each live request coordinate keeps its own declared domain: a name alias resolves once to an ID-pinned handle and never persists as identity; a representation etag guards only the representation revision and neither satisfies nor is satisfied by an expected-runtime-epoch precondition; an event or output cursor is an observation position only and is accepted in no identity, target, precondition, or authority position; an idempotency key is a recovery coordinate only; and a runtime epoch is expressible only as an expected-value precondition and never as an assignable field.
entries.rationale: Q1: the fact is the declared type of each request coordinate at the boundary that decodes it, complete at the live request surface. Q2: owner was `core` in the drafts and moves to `live` under Criterion O, because the fact is the declared type of each request coordinate at its own caller station. Q3: L0 is the decoding station and the last point at which a wrong-domain coordinate can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the caller's live request. Merged from indices 9, 10, and 11 (L2.D12 -- four entries, one owner, one station, two contradictory dispositions -- plus the L0.D2 output-cursor half). The 10-vs-11 reject/unrepresentable disagreement resolves to reject-at-boundary: raw wire frames, native extensions, and adapter ingress can still present a wrong-domain coordinate. Index 48 (OPA, canonical request identity includes transport or presentation fields) is not merged -- its fact set is the composition of the canonical digest backing the idempotency binding, a Core durable record rather than a coordinate domain, so it stays separate at `core`, L0->L0. The Process-ID / output-cursor half is not filed here, because output cursors live at `process.status.output.cursor` on the exec branch and L0 and E1 are mutually unreachable; it becomes A5.
entries.traversal: live Sandbox mutation and observation request traversal
entries.remediation: Resolve the alias once and pin the returned Sandbox ID; evaluate etag and expected runtime epoch as independent preconditions; carry cursors only in observation requests.

entries.title: Snapshot manifest digest substituted for Snapshot identity
entries.statement: Every Snapshot-targeted operation identifies its target by Snapshot ID, and the manifest digest remains an integrity coordinate that resolves no resource.
entries.rationale: Q1: the fact needed is the declared Snapshot target variant, complete at the live request surface. Q2: the Snapshot target union is a Core control-plane fact, but under Criterion O the invalid state is an expressible Snapshot-targeted request at its own caller station, so the owner is `live`. Q3: L0, the station that decodes the sealed target. Q4: no other operation commits it. Disposition is unrepresentable because the Snapshot target admits only a Snapshot ID, and distinct Snapshots may legitimately share a digest.
entries.traversal: Snapshot-targeted live request traversal
entries.remediation: Target Snapshots by Snapshot ID and use the manifest digest only to verify retained content integrity.

entries.title: Deleted or stale Snapshot handle retargeted to equal content
entries.statement: A Snapshot ID that no longer resolves returns a typed target-not-found result and is never resolved to a different Snapshot with equal manifest digest or equivalent content.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the requested Snapshot ID and the durable Snapshot record set including tombstones. Q2: the Snapshot record set including its tombstones is a Core durable record consulted here, but under Criterion O the invalid state is an expressible live request at its own caller station, so the owner is `live`. Q3: L0, because acceptance already binds the operation to a resource the caller never named. Q4: the retarget is committed by this request. It is expressible because content-addressed fallback is a plausible implementation choice, so it must be rejected rather than excluded by type.
entries.traversal: Snapshot-targeted live request traversal
entries.remediation: Resolve Snapshot targets only by exact retained identity and return target-not-found for retired IDs.

entries.title: Operation accepted without the exact target its kind seals
entries.statement: Every accepted Operation records exactly the tagged target variant its operation kind requires, with every coordinate that variant seals present and resolved -- including the exact expected runtime epoch that every runtime-acting live mutation's target variant seals.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the requested method's declared target variant and the coordinates the submitted target carries, complete at live admission. Q2: the protected artefact is the accepted Operation record, a Core durable record, so the owner is `core`. Q3: L0 is the acceptance station and the last point at which an incomplete sealed target can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the request whose acceptance would commit the Operation. Merged from indices 5 and 16 (L1.D13, L2.D17) -- a general rule and its instance filed under different owners at one station.
entries.traversal: live Sandbox, Process, Snapshot, and Fork mutation request traversal
entries.remediation: Supply the tagged target variant declared for the requested method with all sealed coordinates populated, including the expected runtime epoch observed on the handle.

entries.title: Process-targeted Operation retargeted during retry or reconciliation
entries.statement: A Process-targeted Operation keeps the exact Process ID, Sandbox ID, and runtime epoch committed at its acceptance through every retry, adoption, and reconciliation.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the committed Operation target record and the retarget the retry or reconciliation proposes; both are Core records at the live commit station. Q2: durable Operation records are Core. Q3: L1 is where the proposed rewrite would be committed and is therefore the last correct refusal point on this traversal. Q4: a system-originated reconciliation is filed at the same phase as its caller-originated twin, because origin is attribution and not an information set.
entries.traversal: Signal or Terminate live commit and reconciliation traversal
entries.remediation: Reconcile only against the target committed at acceptance and create a linked successor Operation for any different target.

entries.title: Runtime-replacing result omits its previous or resulting epoch
entries.statement: Every Operation result that replaces or creates a runtime records both the previous runtime epoch, or its explicit absence, and the resulting runtime epoch.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the epoch held before this mutation and the epoch it committed, both present in Core records at the result-commit station; no post-launch observation is required, so this is not observed conformance. Q2: the Operation result record is Core. Q3: L1 is the commit that publishes the result; after it the caller can only infer continuity from mutable status. Q4: this result belongs to the live mutation whose traversal is described.
entries.traversal: live Sandbox mutation result-commit traversal
entries.remediation: Record both the previous and resulting runtime epochs on every runtime-replacing or runtime-creating result.

entries.title: Attachment continuity conflated with runtime continuity
entries.statement: Every lifecycle Operation able to change client attachment reports an explicit attachment outcome equivalent to preserved or reconnect-required, and that outcome never decides, substitutes for, or is decided by the runtime epoch.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the attachment observation and the epoch decision recorded on the same result, both available at the result-commit station. Q2: the result record and epoch decision are Core. Q3: L1, because after the result is published a missing or conflated attachment outcome cannot be distinguished from preserved continuity. Q4: the conflation is committed by this Operation's own result.
entries.traversal: live Sandbox mutation result-commit traversal
entries.remediation: Report attachment continuity as its own non-identity outcome and decide the epoch solely from proven runtime continuity.

entries.title: Process record not permanently bound to one Sandbox runtime
entries.statement: Every accepted Process receives a newly allocated Core Process ID permanently bound to exactly one Sandbox ID and runtime epoch, and that binding is never rewritten.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Exec request's runtime reference and the Process identity allocation record, both complete at the exec admission station. Q2: durable Process identity is Core. Q3: E0 is the last station where the binding can still be refused before the Process handle is published to the caller. Q4: a later rebinding attempt by reconciliation is a different act but consults this same committed binding, so it is defensively revalidated rather than separately filed here.
entries.traversal: Exec acceptance traversal
entries.remediation: Allocate a fresh Core Process ID bound to the exact requested Sandbox ID and epoch, and never rebind it.

entries.title: Native execution identifier used as durable public identity
entries.statement: Native PIDs, provider execution identifiers, provider resource identifiers, and VMM identities are recorded only as scoped decoded observations and never become or resolve durable public Sandbox, runtime, Process, Operation, or Snapshot identity.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the native identifiers the driver decodes and the public identity domains they are being written into; both are complete at the decoding boundary. Q2: decoding native evidence is the driver/provider boundary, which is runtime. Q3: D0 is the last station before decoded values reach authoritative Core records. Q4: the substitution is committed by the driver on this effect traversal, not by the caller's request.
entries.traversal: driver decoding and effect-commit traversal
entries.remediation: Keep native identifiers in scoped protected evidence and resolve public resources only through Core-allocated identities.

entries.title: Runtime epoch accepted as Create input
entries.statement: The canonical Create request expresses no runtime epoch, leaving the first epoch server-allocated output-only state that no caller, native extension, or adapter can set, preserve, or reset.
entries.rationale: Q1: the fact needed is the canonical Create request schema, complete at the create request surface. Q2: the creation request surface owns its input schema. Q3: C0 is the boundary that decodes the canonical request. Q4: no other operation commits it. Disposition is unrepresentable because the supported create surface, including its native-extension slots, offers no epoch-carrying field.
entries.traversal: CreateSandbox request traversal
entries.remediation: Read the allocated epoch from the Create result instead of attempting to supply one.

entries.title: Runtime epoch written by a live request
entries.statement: A live request expresses the runtime epoch only as an expected-value precondition and never as an assignable field able to set, reset, preserve, or decrement it.
entries.rationale: Q1: the fact needed is the live request schema and the read-only status of the epoch, complete at the live request surface. Q2: the live request surface owns its input schema. Q3: L0 is the decoding boundary for live requests. Q4: no other operation commits it. Disposition is unrepresentable because every live request type carries the epoch only in a precondition position.
entries.traversal: live Sandbox mutation request traversal
entries.remediation: Use the epoch as a precondition only and let the Core allocate every new runtime epoch.

entries.title: Sandbox name mutated after Create
entries.statement: The Sandbox name is fixed at Create, and no metadata, expiration, or other live update request can express a replacement name.
entries.rationale: Q1: the fact needed is the update request schema for the two representation methods, complete at the live request surface. Q2: those request surfaces are live. Q3: L0 is where the update request is decoded. Q4: no other operation commits it. Disposition is unrepresentable because the metadata and expiration requests carry no name field at all, which is what prevents hidden release and rename races.
entries.traversal: UpdateSandboxMetadata and SetSandboxExpiration request traversal
entries.remediation: Create a new Sandbox with the desired alias rather than attempting to rename an existing one.

entries.title: Authoritative Core commit by a stale authority epoch
entries.statement: Every authoritative Core-state commit validates the complete capability of Sandbox ID, runtime epoch, and authority epoch against the durable authority high-water mark and commits only under the current authority epoch.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the presented capability triple and the durable authority high-water mark, both Core records requiring no external probe. Q2: authority fencing is Core. Q3: D0 is the effect-commit boundary and the last station where refusing still prevents an obsolete actor's write from becoming authoritative. Q4: the commit belongs to whichever actor presents the capability, so this entry is authoritative at D0 with defensive revalidation hooks at R0, R1, L1, E1, and T0.
entries.traversal: driver effect-commit traversal, defensively revalidated at every later commit station
entries.remediation: Validate the full capability against the current authority epoch before every authoritative commit and reject stale holders.

entries.title: Stale provider event treated as serialization authority
entries.statement: A decoded provider, host, or VMM event is retained as non-authoritative evidence and is refused as a state transition whenever the authority epoch it belongs to is no longer current.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the event, the authority epoch it was produced under, and the current authority epoch, all present at the decoding boundary. Q2: decoding provider events is the driver/provider boundary, which is runtime; the Core commit rule is a separate two-owner seam. Q3: D0 is the decoding boundary and the last station where the event can still be downgraded to evidence. Q4: the offending act is the driver's decode, not the caller's request.
entries.traversal: driver provider-event decoding traversal
entries.remediation: Reject the transition by authority epoch and retain the event only as protected non-authoritative evidence.

entries.title: Successor effect authority granted without fencing or drain proof
entries.statement: The Core grants a successor actor effect authority only after the target is proven, for this exact handoff, to validate the fencing token atomically or to provide a product-verifiable predecessor drain or termination boundary.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the current external target's fencing and drain capability for this handoff plus the predecessor's outstanding authority; the target capability is external state the product does not own, which is what makes this a preflight rather than a boundary rejection. Q2: granting effect authority is Core. Q3: D0 is the last station before the successor could produce an effect. Q4: the grant is made on this traversal before the successor acts, so it is not deferred to the successor's own traversal.
entries.traversal: authority handoff preflight traversal preceding driver dispatch
entries.remediation: Prove atomic target fencing or a verifiable predecessor drain for the handoff, or quarantine and reconcile instead of granting authority.

entries.title: Driver claims exclusive effect authority without target fencing support
entries.statement: A driver declares for each effect boundary it exposes whether the target validates its fencing token atomically or offers a verifiable drain boundary, and refuses to dispatch an exclusive effect when it can prove neither.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the target's current fencing behaviour and the driver's declared effect contract, checked immediately before dispatch; validity turns on current external state, so this is a preflight. Q2: the effect boundary and its fencing mechanics are the driver/provider boundary. Q3: D0, because after dispatch exclusivity can no longer be established. Q4: the driver commits the violation on its own dispatch traversal, distinct from the Core grant that precedes it.
entries.traversal: driver dispatch traversal
entries.remediation: Declare the fencing mechanism per effect boundary and refuse exclusive dispatch when neither atomic fencing nor a verifiable drain exists.

entries.title: Unfenced handoff reported as a definite outcome
entries.statement: When a handoff cannot establish exclusive effect authority, the affected resources are quarantined or reconciled and the Operation retains its ambiguous terminal outcome rather than a definite success or failure.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the post-handoff evidence about whether the predecessor can still act, which exists only after the launch or handoff has run; the outcome is therefore provable only from observed conformance. Q2: terminal outcomes are Core. Q3: R1 is the terminalization station on this traversal and the last point at which a definite outcome can be withheld. Q4: reconciliation and adoption resolving the ambiguity are filed at exactly this phase, since origin is attribution rather than an information set.
entries.traversal: launch, handoff, and reconciliation terminalization traversal
entries.remediation: Quarantine or reconcile the affected resources and publish the ambiguity variant naming the fencing proof Core lacks.

entries.title: Driver retry or adoption without native idempotency or exact adoption proof
entries.statement: A driver retries the same external effect only under the provider's own idempotency token for that effect and adopts an existing external execution only with exact proof of its external identity, target, runtime epoch, and fencing.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the declared effect class, the provider's currently available idempotency token, and the discoverable external identity; these depend on current external provider state, so the check is a preflight decided before mutation. Q2: native idempotency and adoption identity live at the driver/provider boundary. Q3: D0, because after dispatch a blind retry has already duplicated the effect. Q4: this is the driver half of a two-owner seam whose Core half records the recovery classification on its own traversal.
entries.traversal: driver retry and adoption traversal
entries.remediation: Retry only with the provider's own idempotency token, adopt only under exact identity and fencing proof, and otherwise reconcile.

entries.title: Provider status alone justifies a Core outcome
entries.statement: Every driver declares which native identities, state observations, fencing results, and supervision facts justify each Core outcome variant it may report, and reports no variant whose declared evidence it did not obtain.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the driver's declared evidence contract and the evidence actually held, both complete at the decoding boundary and independent of any later observation. Q2: the evidence contract belongs to the driver/provider boundary. Q3: D0 is where a variant is selected, so it is the last station at which an unjustified variant can be refused. Q4: the driver commits the violation; the separate rule that provider acknowledgement is not the Core postcondition is a different fact set on the launch traversal.
entries.traversal: driver evidence-decoding and outcome-selection traversal
entries.remediation: Declare required evidence per outcome variant and map status-only responses to the ambiguity variant instead.

entries.title: Create rejected after durable creation intent exists
entries.statement: A CreateSandbox call returns a request rejection only while Core proves that no Operation, no dispatchable effect intent, no external invocation, and no recoverable accepted result exists; otherwise it is accepted and every later outcome is embedded in its Operation.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the four acceptance-proof conditions over Core's own durable records, complete at the creation acceptance station without needing the resolved target runtime. Q2: durable acceptance records are Core. Q3: D0 is the last station on this traversal before an external effect exists, after which a rejection would deny a committed acceptance. Q4: the rejection would be returned by this same call.
entries.traversal: CreateSandbox acceptance traversal
entries.remediation: Return a request rejection only before the acceptance commit and afterwards report every outcome inside the Operation.

entries.title: Live request rejected after durable mutation intent exists
entries.statement: A live Sandbox, Process-signal, Snapshot, or Fork mutation returns a request rejection only while Core proves that no Operation, no dispatchable effect intent, no external invocation, and no recoverable accepted result exists.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the same four acceptance-proof conditions read over this request's own durable records at the live admission station. Q2: durable acceptance is Core. Q3: L1 is the acceptance commit and the last station at which a rejection is still truthful. Q4: the create and exec surfaces never traverse L0, so filing one entry for all three would assert coverage on components that never see this pair.
entries.traversal: live Sandbox mutation acceptance traversal
entries.remediation: Prove the four acceptance conditions before returning a request rejection and otherwise accept and report through the Operation.

entries.title: Exec rejected after durable execution intent exists
entries.statement: An Exec returns a request rejection only while Core proves that no Process, no dispatchable effect intent, no external invocation, and no recoverable accepted result exists.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the four acceptance-proof conditions read over the Process record and effect intent at the exec admission station. Q2: durable acceptance is Core. Q3: E1 is the Process acceptance commit and the last station at which a rejection is still truthful. Q4: the exec traversal never enters L0 or L1, so this is a separate entry from the live-surface rule.
entries.traversal: Exec acceptance traversal
entries.remediation: Prove the four acceptance conditions before returning a request rejection and otherwise accept and report through the Process.

entries.title: Launch dispatched before its acceptance commit
entries.statement: No launch or other external creation effect is dispatched before Core atomically commits the Operation handle, canonical request and digest, preallocated Sandbox identity, idempotency binding, allocated runtime epoch, effect intent, and effect-authority epoch.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the contents of the acceptance commit, all of which exist at the creation acceptance station; the resolved target runtime value is not needed to decide whether the commit happened first, so C0 is the earliest complete station rather than D0. Q2: the durable acceptance record is Core. Q3: D0 is the last station before the external effect is invoked. Q4: the dispatch belongs to this create traversal.
entries.traversal: CreateSandbox acceptance and launch-dispatch traversal
entries.remediation: Commit the full acceptance record, epoch allocation, and effect intent atomically before invoking any provider or driver effect.

entries.title: Live effect dispatched before its acceptance commit
entries.statement: No live external effect is dispatched before Core atomically commits the Operation handle, canonical request and digest, sealed target with every applicable freshness precondition, idempotency binding, effect intent, and effect-authority epoch.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the acceptance-commit contents for this live mutation, complete at the live admission station. Q2: the durable acceptance record is Core. Q3: L1 is the commit that must precede dispatch, so it is the last correct refusal point. Q4: the dispatch is performed for this same live request.
entries.traversal: live Sandbox mutation acceptance and dispatch traversal
entries.remediation: Commit the acceptance record and effect intent atomically before dispatching the live effect.

entries.title: Exec dispatched before its acceptance commit
entries.statement: No Exec is dispatched before Core atomically commits the Core Process ID, canonical request and digest, exact Sandbox runtime reference, idempotency binding, launch token, effect intent, and effect-authority epoch.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the exec acceptance-commit contents, complete at the exec admission station. Q2: the durable Process record is Core. Q3: E1 is the commit that must precede dispatch; after dispatch an unrecorded execution cannot be reconciled by launch token. Q4: the dispatch belongs to this exec traversal, which never enters the live pair.
entries.traversal: Exec acceptance and dispatch traversal
entries.remediation: Durably allocate the Process ID and launch token and commit the acceptance record before dispatching the execution.

entries.title: Create replay rejected against current mutable state
entries.statement: Idempotency lookup for a CreateSandbox request runs immediately after authorization and canonicalization and before target-state, capability, concurrency, capacity, and quota checks, so an equal replay recovers its original handle.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the idempotency coordinate, the stored binding, and the declared admission order, all complete at the create request surface. Q2: the idempotency binding and the declared ordered admission sequence are the control plane's own durable artefacts, so under Criterion O the owner is `core`. Q3: C0, because once a mutable-state error is returned the caller has lost the recovery path to its original handle. Q4: the misordering is committed by this request.
entries.traversal: CreateSandbox admission traversal
entries.remediation: Resolve idempotency before evaluating mutable lifecycle, capacity, or quota preconditions.

entries.title: Live replay rejected against current mutable state
entries.statement: Idempotency lookup for a live mutation runs immediately after authorization and canonicalization and before lifecycle-state, concurrency, capacity, and quota checks, so a retry of an accepted mutation recovers its original Operation instead of being rejected as invalid for the current state.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the idempotency coordinate, the stored binding, and the declared admission order at the live request surface. Q2: the stored binding is a Core durable record, which also makes this a boundary rejection rather than a dynamic preflight. Q3: L0, because a state-based rejection already destroys the recovery path. Q4: the misordering belongs to this request; the classic instance is a retried Start arriving after the Sandbox is already running.
entries.traversal: live Sandbox mutation admission traversal
entries.remediation: Look up the idempotency coordinate before any mutable-state check and return the original Operation on equal replay.

entries.title: Exec replay rejected against current mutable state
entries.statement: Idempotency lookup for an Exec runs immediately after authorization and canonicalization and before execution-admission, concurrency, capacity, and quota checks, so an equal replay recovers its original Process.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the idempotency coordinate, the stored binding, and the declared admission order at the exec request surface. Q2: the stored binding is a Core durable record. Q3: E0, because an admission-based rejection loses the caller's route back to the accepted Process. Q4: the exec traversal never enters L0, so it needs its own entry.
entries.traversal: Exec admission traversal
entries.remediation: Resolve the Exec idempotency coordinate before evaluating execution admission or capacity.

entries.title: Live idempotency coordinate rebound to a different intent
entries.statement: One authenticated scope, method, and idempotency key binds exactly one canonical request digest for its published recovery window, so an equal replay returns the original Operation and a conflicting replay is rejected without dispatching any effect.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the stored binding of coordinate to canonical digest to handle and the incoming digest; the consulted fact is a Core durable record, not request content, which fixes the owner as core rather than the request surface. Q2: the idempotency binding is a Core durable record. Q3: L0, because acceptance under a rebound key already produces a second effect. Q4: the create surface never traverses L0, so the creation-scope half of this rule cannot be asserted here and is filed as its own entry at `199`.
entries.traversal: live Sandbox mutation admission traversal
entries.remediation: Reject the conflicting replay with the typed idempotency conflict and dispatch nothing, or submit a new key.

entries.title: Exec idempotency coordinate rebound to a different intent
entries.statement: One authenticated scope, method, and idempotency key binds exactly one canonical Exec digest for its published recovery window, so an equal replay returns the original Process and a conflicting replay is rejected without dispatching any execution.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the stored Exec binding and the incoming canonical digest, both Core durable records. Q2: the binding is Core. Q3: E0, because acceptance under a rebound key already launches a second execution. Q4: the exec traversal never enters L0, so the live entry cannot assert coverage here.
entries.traversal: Exec admission traversal
entries.remediation: Reject the conflicting Exec replay with the typed idempotency conflict and dispatch no execution.

entries.title: Canonical request identity includes transport or presentation fields
entries.statement: The canonical request digest excludes transport-only fields, trace identifiers, and correlation metadata, and includes every field able to change target, authority, effect, policy, result, or postcondition.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the request encoding and the declared canonicalization domain, complete at the live request surface where the digest is computed. Q2: the canonical digest is a Core durable-record input. Q3: L0, because the digest is stored with the acceptance commit and a wrong domain makes both false conflicts and false replays permanent. Q4: the miscanonicalization is committed by the request being admitted; correlation metadata carries no deduplication or authorization meaning by construction.
entries.traversal: live Sandbox mutation canonicalization traversal
entries.remediation: Canonicalize over semantic fields only and keep trace and correlation metadata outside the digest.

entries.title: Retired create idempotency record silently authorizes a new effect
entries.statement: A CreateSandbox replay whose idempotency coordinate is retired or older than the published recovery window returns a recovery error carrying its tagged prior-acceptance evidence and never becomes a new accepted creation.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the coordinate age, the published recovery window, the acceptance tombstone, and the retained result reference, all Core records available at the create request surface. Q2: the acceptance tombstone, the published recovery window, and the retained result reference are the control plane's own durable artefacts, so under Criterion O the owner is `core`. Q3: C0, because accepting it as new already authorizes a second creation. Q4: the conversion would be committed by this request.
entries.traversal: CreateSandbox admission traversal
entries.remediation: Return the expired-record recovery error with its prior-acceptance evidence and require operator or observation recovery.

entries.title: Retired live idempotency record silently authorizes a new mutation
entries.statement: A live mutation replay whose idempotency coordinate is retired or older than the published recovery window returns a recovery error carrying its tagged prior-acceptance evidence and never becomes a new accepted mutation.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the coordinate age, the published window, tombstones, and any retained result reference, all Core durable records. Q2: retention and tombstones are Core. Q3: L0, because acceptance is itself the silent conversion. Q4: the create and exec surfaces never traverse this pair and therefore carry their own entries.
entries.traversal: live Sandbox mutation admission traversal
entries.remediation: Return the expired-record recovery error and never treat an expired coordinate as proof that no effect occurred.

entries.title: Retired exec idempotency record silently authorizes a new execution
entries.statement: An Exec replay whose idempotency coordinate is retired or older than the published recovery window returns a recovery error carrying its tagged prior-acceptance evidence and never becomes a new accepted execution.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the coordinate age, the published window, tombstones, and any retained Process reference, all Core durable records. Q2: retention and tombstones are Core. Q3: E0, because acceptance already launches a second execution. Q4: the exec traversal never enters L0, so this is filed separately.
entries.traversal: Exec admission traversal
entries.remediation: Return the expired-record recovery error and require explicit observation before any new execution is formed.

entries.title: Terminal failed Operation automatically replayed as a new attempt
entries.statement: An accepted terminal failure is recovered as the original Operation's outcome, and creating a genuinely new attempt requires a new idempotency key together with operation-specific authority to attempt it again.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the stored idempotency binding and the terminal outcome of the bound Operation, both Core durable records at the admission station. Q2: durable Operation records are Core. Q3: L0, because acceptance of the replay as a new attempt is itself the unauthorized second effect. Q4: a system-originated replay is filed at exactly the phase of its caller-originated twin, since origin is attribution and not an information set.
entries.traversal: live Sandbox mutation admission traversal
entries.remediation: Return the original failed Operation on replay and require a new key plus explicit authority for a fresh attempt.

entries.title: Cancellation request recorded as a cancellation fact
entries.statement: An accepted cancellation request monotonically records cancel_requested on the existing Operation and allocates no new Operation, leaving that Operation the sole authority for its terminal outcome.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the existing Operation record and the cancellation intent commit, both Core records at the live acceptance station; proving exclusion of the effect is a different fact set carried by the outcome-legality entries. Q2: durable Operation records are Core. Q3: L1 is the intent commit, the last station at which an Operation-of-Operation or a premature cancelled outcome can still be refused. Q4: the terminal outcome is decided on the target Operation's own traversal, not here.
entries.traversal: CancelOperation acceptance traversal
entries.remediation: Record cancel_requested on the existing Operation and let that Operation publish the terminal outcome once exclusion is proven.

entries.title: Representation and idempotency result committed separately
entries.statement: An atomic Core-record update commits the new representation, its resulting revision, the idempotency binding, and the recoverable committed response in one commit, so an equal replay returns that response without applying the update again.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the prior revision, the requested representation, and the idempotency binding, all Core records complete at the live admission station. Q2: Core-owned representation records are Core. Q3: L1 is the single commit point; splitting it is only observable there. Q4: this update class has no dispatch or later traversal on which the split could be caught.
entries.traversal: UpdateSandboxMetadata and SetSandboxExpiration acceptance traversal
entries.remediation: Commit representation, resulting revision, idempotency binding, and committed response in one atomic write.

entries.title: Non-atomic record storage exposed for atomic update methods
entries.statement: A Core deployment whose record storage cannot commit the representation and its idempotency result atomically fails admission for the atomic-update methods rather than advertising them or substituting a durable Operation.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the configured storage's declared transactional capability and the method set being advertised, both complete at operator configuration. Q2: deployment storage selection and capability admission are operator-owned. Q3: O0 is the operator resolution boundary and the last station before the method is advertised. Q4: the caller's later request is a different traversal that would already be too late, so the refusal is filed here.
entries.traversal: operator configuration and capability-admission traversal
entries.remediation: Fail build, startup, or capability admission closed instead of advertising the atomic-update methods on non-transactional storage.

entries.title: External effect attempted before its recovery classification is recorded
entries.statement: Before each external effect attempt on the launch traversal Core durably records the attempt with its exact parameters together with one of the four locked recovery classes: no durable intent, provider idempotency token available, external identity discoverable for adoption, or none available.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the effect parameters plus the provider's currently available idempotency scope and identity discoverability, which are external provider state and must be determined before mutation rather than after. Q2: the durable effect-attempt record and its classification are Core. Q3: R0 is the last station before the launch result is interpreted, after which an unclassified attempt cannot be safely retried or adopted. Q4: the driver's obligation to prove native idempotency or exact adoption is the other half of a two-owner seam and is filed on the driver's own boundary.
entries.traversal: external effect-attempt traversal preceding launch dispatch
entries.remediation: Persist the effect-attempt record with its recovery class before dispatch, and report ambiguity with quarantine when no class applies.

entries.title: Launch Operation terminalized beyond its proven evidence
entries.statement: A launch Operation commits `succeeded` only when every possibility remaining under Core's evidence satisfies its exact success postcondition with cancellation `notRequested` or proven `lost`, commits `failed` or `cancelled` only when no remaining possibility satisfies that postcondition, every possibility has `mutationAuthority = quiesced`, and residual effects are known, and otherwise commits `unknown` with its exact ambiguity variant.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the accumulated knowledge set for one accepted launch attempt, its cancellation causality, and the method-specific success predicate; that set is complete only at R1, where the launched runtime has been observed and probed. Q2: Core owns terminal Operation outcomes. Q3: R1 is the station that publishes the terminal outcome, so refusing an unproven arm there is still a correct product implementation. Q4: this is the launch traversal's own outcome, not a later operation's. `observed-conformance` because arm legality is provable only from post-launch evidence; the `mutationAuthority = quiesced` predicate and the cancellation causality lattice are required witnesses rather than separate entries. Filed as a self-pair on the launch traversal, never as C0->R1.
entries.traversal: Create/Start/Restore launch traversal terminalizing at R1
entries.remediation: Commit `unknown` with its exact ambiguity variant unless the evidence proves the whole predicate of the chosen arm, including quiesced mutation authority and known residuals.

entries.title: Live mutation Operation terminalized beyond its proven evidence
entries.statement: A live Sandbox, Snapshot, or Process-targeted mutation Operation commits `succeeded`, `failed`, or `cancelled` only when its exact evidence predicate for that arm holds over every remaining possibility, and otherwise commits `unknown`; a received cancellation request, an unresolved `cancellation = requested`, an internal timer expiry, or an RPC deadline never selects a definite arm.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the knowledge set, cancellation causality, and success predicate for one accepted live mutation; complete only at L1, where that mutation's effect evidence exists. Q2: Core owns terminal Operation outcomes. Q3: L1 publishes the outcome and is the last station on this traversal at which refusing an unproven arm is correct. Q4: the live mutation's own traversal. A single L1->T0 filing was rejected because it would bind the launch and exec branches to a pair they do not traverse in that direction; per-station filing keeps the coverage claim true. `observed-conformance` because the arm is provable only after the effect was attempted.
entries.traversal: One live mutation against an existing Sandbox, terminalizing at L1
entries.remediation: Leave the Operation `unknown` while cancellation is unresolved or mutation authority may still act; never promote a cancellation request or deadline into a terminal arm.

entries.title: Exec dispatch outcome committed beyond its proven evidence
entries.statement: An accepted Exec dispatch commits a terminal Process outcome only when every possibility remaining under Core's evidence satisfies that outcome's exact predicate with quiesced dispatch authority and known residuals; every other nonempty knowledge set leaves the Process in reconcilable `unknown`.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the evidence set for one accepted execution attempt against the Process success predicate; they first exist at E1, after dispatch. Q2: Core owns the durable Process record and which outcome it may commit; the driver's decoding of native termination evidence into a typed arm is a separate runtime-owned rule. Q3: E1 is where the Process record is terminalized, so refusal there is still correct. Q4: the Exec traversal's own outcome. `observed-conformance` because the knowledge set exists only after the launch effect was attempted.
entries.traversal: One Exec request inside an existing Sandbox, terminalizing at E1
entries.remediation: Keep the Process `unknown` and reconcilable until exact evidence bound to the same launch token proves the committed outcome.

entries.title: Teardown Operation terminalized beyond its proven evidence
entries.statement: A Stop, Delete, or other teardown Operation commits `succeeded`, `failed`, or `cancelled` only when its exact evidence predicate holds over every remaining possibility, and otherwise commits `unknown`; a cleanup attempt, a missing observation, native resource absence, or a provider acknowledgement never substitutes for cleanup completion, target absence, descendant quiescence, or the required Core postcondition.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the teardown attempt's final evidence set, its residual obligations, and its cancellation causality; complete only at T0, the sink where teardown evidence is final. Q2: Core owns terminal Operation outcomes. Q3: T0 publishes the outcome and is the last station on this traversal. Q4: the teardown traversal's own outcome; cleanup carried out by a later linked Operation is filed on that Operation's traversal. `observed-conformance` because absence and quiescence are provable only from observed teardown evidence.
entries.traversal: Stop/Delete teardown traversal terminalizing at T0
entries.remediation: Report `unknown` while any descendant, orphan, or cleanup obligation may still act; never infer absence from a missing observation or an accepted cleanup call.

entries.title: Terminal Operation result rewritten
entries.statement: An Operation's committed terminal outcome and its payload are immutable, and later evidence, reconciliation, adoption, quarantine, or cleanup may only append a linked successor record that references the unchanged predecessor.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the existing terminal Operation record and the proposed write; both are Core durable records and no new observation is needed to refuse the rewrite. Q2: Core owns durable records and terminal outcomes. Q3: R1 is the launch-branch reconciliation/adoption traversal's own resolution station and the last point on that traversal at which the rewrite can be refused; `origin` is attribution, so a system-originated reconciliation is filed at the station its caller-originated twin traverses, and reconciliations that resolve at L1 or T0 are filed as their own per-station siblings rather than asserted here. Q4: the offending write belongs to the reconciling traversal, which is the traversal described here. `reject-at-boundary` rather than `observed-conformance`: immutability is decided from two stored records, not proved after launch; the reconciler's separate evidence-gathering discipline is a different obligation. The legal form -- appending a linked successor resolution record -- is this entry's required valid witness.
entries.traversal: Launch-branch reconciliation/adoption traversal resolving against an existing terminal Operation, at R1
entries.remediation: Append a linked successor resolution Operation instead of rewriting the predecessor's terminal outcome.

entries.title: Compensation represented as rollback
entries.statement: A compensating effect recorded on the teardown or cleanup traversal is recorded as a new forward effect with its own durable record, evidence, and outcome, and never as erasure, reversal, or negation of the compensated Operation's external history -- including when in-sandbox state was restored from a Snapshot or filesystem capture.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the compensated Operation's terminal record and the compensating effect's own record; the representation rule reads those two records at final evidence, so T0 is the earliest station where both exist. Q2: Core owns durable records and terminal outcomes; the D0-time declaration of a compensable effect class is a different fact set and is absorbed by the recovery-classification entry. Q3: T0 is the sink where the compensation record is published, and refusing a rollback representation there is still correct. Q4: the compensating traversal's own record. `reject-at-boundary` because the over-claim is visible in the two records without any further probe. The forbidden inference `filesystem restoration as external-effect rollback` is carried here as a required invalid witness: restoring in-sandbox state never claims that an email, network call, or payment was undone.
entries.traversal: Compensating-effect traversal recording against a prior Operation on the teardown or cleanup traversal, at T0
entries.remediation: Record compensation as a new linked forward effect with its own outcome; never mark the compensated Operation or its external effects as reversed.

entries.title: Observation deadline mutating or terminalizing its target
entries.statement: An observation, wait, or watch deadline ends only that observation and never cancels, mutates, terminalizes, requests cancellation of, or advances the durable state of the observed Sandbox, Operation, or Snapshot.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the observation's own deadline and the identity of the observed durable record; both are complete at the observation request surface, and no effect evidence is required. Q2: Core owns the durable records whose state the deadline must not touch. Q3: L0 is where the observation is served and returned; an observation has no acceptance commit, so refusing the mutation there is the only correct implementation. Q4: an expiry-driven state change caused by a different operation is filed on that operation's traversal. `reject-at-boundary` because the deadline and the record are both known locally.
entries.traversal: One observation (Get/List/Wait) against an existing Sandbox, Operation, or Snapshot, at L0
entries.remediation: Return the observation result with the latest resource and an explicit condition-met flag; leave the observed record unchanged.

entries.title: Interrupted effect attempt resolved without its committed intent
entries.statement: An effect attempt interrupted after dispatch is resolved only by evidence bound to its own committed effect intent, launch token, exact external identity, and authority epoch, and is otherwise terminalized `unknown`; it is never resolved by a fresh attempt, by a differently identified native execution, or by assuming the attempt's outcome.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the durably committed effect intent, the dispatch record, and whatever evidence can be bound to them; they first exist together at R0, immediately after dispatch. Q2: Core owns the durable effect-attempt record and the terminal outcome; the driver's declaration and proof of native idempotency or exact adoption is a separate runtime-owned rule at D0. Q3: R1 is the last station on this traversal at which refusing an unbound resolution is still correct, because the outcome is published there. Q4: the interrupted attempt's own traversal. `reject-at-boundary`: the binding check compares recorded identities and needs no external-state preflight.
entries.traversal: Launch traversal resuming an interrupted effect attempt between dispatch (R0) and terminalization (R1)
entries.remediation: Reconcile using the same committed intent and launch token, or terminalize the Operation `unknown`; never dispatch a second attempt to resolve the first.

entries.title: Ambiguous launch outcome used as successor-effect permission
entries.statement: A launch Operation that terminalized `unknown` authorizes no relaunch, replacement, or adoption effect against the same intent, and any successor launch requires an independently proven fencing boundary, an exact adoption identity, or a newly authorized caller request with its own accepted intent.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the published terminal `unknown` outcome and the proposed successor effect's authorization basis; both exist at R1 once the outcome is committed. Q2: Core owns terminal outcomes and effect authority. Q3: R1 is the station that would grant the successor, so refusing there is correct. Q4: where the successor is itself a fully separate accepted operation, its admission is filed on that operation's traversal; this entry constrains only the inference drawn at the ambiguous launch's own resolution station. `reject-at-boundary` because the terminal record and the successor's proof set are both Core-held.
entries.traversal: Launch traversal at its terminalization station, R1
entries.remediation: Gather fencing or exact adoption proof, or require a new caller request with a new idempotency key; never treat `unknown` as permission to launch again.

entries.title: Ambiguous live outcome used as successor-effect permission
entries.statement: A live mutation Operation that terminalized `unknown` authorizes no repeated, replacement, or compensating external effect against the same target and epoch until fenced evidence, exact adoption identity, or a newly authorized request establishes the successor's authority.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the live mutation's terminal `unknown` record and the proposed successor's authority basis; complete at L1. Q2: Core owns terminal outcomes and effect authority. Q3: L1 is the resolution station for this traversal. Q4: a genuinely new caller-authored mutation is a different traversal and is admitted on its own facts; this entry forbids only Core-initiated replacement from the ambiguity itself. Filed separately from the launch station because a single filing would claim that the launch and exec components revalidate a pair they do not traverse. `reject-at-boundary`.
entries.traversal: One live mutation against an existing Sandbox, at its terminalization station L1
entries.remediation: Quarantine or reconcile the target under a linked Operation; do not re-dispatch the same external effect on the strength of the ambiguity.

entries.title: Ambiguous teardown outcome used as cleanup or destruction permission
entries.statement: A Stop or Delete Operation that terminalized `unknown`, or `failed` with residual obligations, authorizes no assumed-complete cleanup, no identity release, and no successor destructive effect until an actor holding current authority durably discharges each exact residual obligation.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the teardown Operation's terminal record, its enumerated residual obligations, and the proposed successor's authority; complete at T0. Q2: Core owns terminal outcomes, retention, and the release of identities. Q3: T0 is the sink where the successor would be authorized. Q4: a later cleanup Operation is a different traversal and carries its own admission facts; this entry constrains only the inference made at the ambiguous teardown's own station. `reject-at-boundary` because both the residual record and the successor's authority are Core-held.
entries.traversal: Stop/Delete teardown traversal at T0
entries.remediation: Keep the residual obligations open and observable, and discharge them under a linked cleanup Operation with current authority before any further destructive effect.

entries.title: Sandbox deletion erasing independently retained records early
entries.statement: A successful Sandbox deletion removes only the live Sandbox aggregate and the live resources covered by that Operation, and every independently retained Operation, Process, output, event, evidence, and Snapshot record remains readable until its own retention contract expires.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the set of resources covered by this Delete Operation and each dependent record's own retention contract; both are Core durable records complete at the deletion proof station. Q2: Core owns retention and durable records. Q3: T0 is where deletion is committed and is therefore the last station at which refusing an over-broad erase is correct. Q4: this is the Delete traversal's own proof obligation, not a later reader's. `reject-at-boundary` rather than `dynamic-preflight` because retention state is a Core durable fact, not current external state.
entries.traversal: DeleteSandbox teardown traversal at T0
entries.remediation: Scope deletion to the live aggregate and its covered live resources; let each retained record expire under its own published retention contract.

entries.title: Delete admitted while a dependent Snapshot is unresolved
entries.statement: DeleteSandbox is admitted only when every dependent Snapshot has been deleted, exported or mirrored into Core-controlled retention, or otherwise proven independent of the Sandbox aggregate.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the Delete request's target and the Core-held dependency and retention-reference set for its Snapshots; both are complete at the request surface before any teardown effect. Q2: the request surface for one operation against an existing Sandbox owns this admission. Q3: L0 is the admission station and the last point at which refusing costs nothing; admitting and then discovering the dependency would already have destroyed retained bytes. Q4: deleting the Snapshots themselves is a different operation filed on its own traversal. Per the retention ruling this is a Delete-traversal ADMISSION obligation and filing it at T0 would be an error. `reject-at-boundary`, not `dynamic-preflight`: the reference set is a Core durable record.
entries.traversal: DeleteSandbox request admission at L0
entries.remediation: Delete, mirror, or prove independent every dependent Snapshot, then reissue Delete.

entries.title: Expiration schedule without an explicit instant and action
entries.statement: A caller-managed Sandbox expiration is either explicit `none` or an exact absolute instant paired with an explicit `stop` or `delete` action, and neither member has a provider-, target-, or service-selected default.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the members of the submitted expiration value itself; nothing outside the request is needed. Q2: `SetSandboxExpiration` is one operation against an existing Sandbox, so the request surface owns the value's shape. Q3: L0 is where the value is accepted; there is no later station on this traversal. Q4: the system Stop or Delete that the schedule later triggers is a different operation filed on its own traversal. `unrepresentable`: the canonical expiration is a closed tagged value, so an instant without an action, or an action without an instant, cannot be constructed by a supported API.
entries.traversal: SetSandboxExpiration atomic Core-record update at L0
entries.remediation: Submit `none` or an absolute instant together with an explicit `stop` or `delete` action.

entries.title: Expiration schedule conflated with a generic TTL
entries.statement: The caller-managed expiration schedule expresses only an absolute Sandbox expiry instant and its action, and never sets, reads, or stands in for maximum age from creation, idle duration, maximum runtime duration, Snapshot retention, or Operation, Process, event, and output retention.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the submitted schedule read against the closed set of distinct lifecycle and retention clock families and their separately declared subjects; all are known at the request surface. Q2: the live request surface owns which fact this operation may set. Q3: L0 is the acceptance station for this atomic Core-record update. Q4: the Artifact-declared ceilings that must not be widened are a different owner's facts and are filed on the Artifact traversal. Distinct from the schedule's own shape rule under Ruling R1: the facts consulted are the other clock families, not the value's members. `reject-at-boundary`.
entries.traversal: SetSandboxExpiration atomic Core-record update at L0
entries.remediation: Set only the absolute expiry instant and action here; express idle, age, runtime-duration, and record-retention policy through their own declared contracts.

entries.title: Bare duration standing for distinct Artifact time contracts
entries.statement: Every Artifact-declared time bound names its exact clock, subject, and enforcement contract, and one bare duration never stands for maximum lifetime, idle timeout, maximum age from creation, maximum runtime duration, or record retention.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the fully expanded Artifact time-bound declarations and their declared subjects; they are complete once imports and profiles are expanded at A0. Q2: the Artifact Definition owns declarative ceilings. Q3: A1 is the final Artifact semantic validator, the last station at which an ambiguous bound can be refused before it crosses the canonical boundary. Q4: the runtime schedule that must not widen a ceiling belongs to the live traversal and is filed there. `reject-at-boundary`: the ambiguity is decidable from the normalized Artifact alone.
entries.traversal: Artifact normalization and semantic validation, A0 to A1
entries.remediation: Declare each time bound under its own named clock and subject; do not reuse one duration field for lifetime, idle, age, and retention.

entries.title: Caller deletion of a retained Operation record
entries.statement: Operation retention is service-enforced and independent of target deletion, and the closed public method surface exposes no caller-facing Operation deletion, purge, or retention-override request.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the closed public method union and the request's method identity; nothing else is consulted. Q2: retention and the durable Operation record whose lifetime the absent method would shorten are Core facts consulted here, but under Criterion O the invalid state is an expressible request at its own caller station, so the owner is `live`. Q3: L0 is the request surface where such a call would arrive, and there is no later station on that traversal. Q4: deleting the Operation's target is a different operation filed on its own traversal, and retention is explicitly independent of it. `unrepresentable`: no supported API constructs a caller Operation deletion.
entries.traversal: Request against an existing Operation resource at L0
entries.remediation: Observe the Operation and let its service-published retention expire; use `CancelOperation` when the intent is to stop nonterminal work.

entries.title: Proven deletion without a durable identity tombstone
entries.statement: A Delete Operation reports success only after durably committing a retained tombstone that preserves the Sandbox identity and its audit coordinates so that the identity can never be reused.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the deletion proof and the tombstone commit; both belong to the Delete traversal and are complete at its proof station. Q2: Core owns durable records, retention, and identity allocation. Q3: T0 is where success is published, so refusing to publish before the tombstone is durable is still correct. Q4: a later creation that would reuse the identity or an unreleased name is a different operation and is filed at its own C0 station; this entry is the Delete-traversal proof obligation that makes that later rule decidable. `reject-at-boundary`.
entries.traversal: DeleteSandbox teardown traversal at T0
entries.remediation: Commit the tombstone and audit coordinates durably as part of the deletion proof, before the Operation reports success.

entries.title: Creation rejection outside the sealed error registry
entries.statement: Every synchronous rejection of a creation request is exactly one variant of the sealed public `RequestError` or `RecoveryError` registry admitted by that method's generated subset, with no catch-all variant, open string reason, arbitrary metadata reason, or provider-defined code.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the sealed registry, this method's exact generated subset, and the variant being emitted; all are known at the creation request surface. Q2: Core owns the closed error registry and the per-method admissibility sets, even though the station is the creation ingress. Q3: C0 is where the creation rejection is authored and returned. Q4: an adapter-added variant is committed by the adapter and is filed on the framework traversal. Filed per surface: one filing would claim that live and exec response encoders revalidate a pair they never traverse. `unrepresentable` because the generated per-method union admits no other value.
entries.traversal: CreateSandbox request ingress and rejection at C0
entries.remediation: Add the condition to the sealed registry and regenerate the method subset, or map it onto an existing admitted variant.

entries.title: Live rejection outside the sealed error registry
entries.statement: Every synchronous rejection of a live Sandbox, Snapshot, or Operation request is exactly one variant of the sealed public `RequestError` or `RecoveryError` registry admitted by that method's generated subset, with no catch-all variant, open string reason, arbitrary metadata reason, or provider-defined code.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the sealed registry, this method's generated subset, and the emitted variant, all present at the live request surface. Q2: Core owns the closed registry and per-method admissibility. Q3: L0 is where the live rejection is authored and returned. Q4: a driver's unrecognized native code is committed at the decoding boundary and is filed on the runtime traversal. Filed separately from the create and exec surfaces so the generated coverage names only components these methods actually traverse. `unrepresentable`.
entries.traversal: One live operation against an existing Sandbox, rejected at L0
entries.remediation: Emit an admitted registry variant for this method, or extend the sealed registry and regenerate every dependent union, mapping, and fixture.

entries.title: Exec or Process-control rejection outside the sealed error registry
entries.statement: Every synchronous rejection of an Exec or sequenced Process-control request is exactly one variant of the sealed public `RequestError` or `RecoveryError` registry admitted by that method's generated subset, with no catch-all variant, open string reason, arbitrary metadata reason, or provider-defined code.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the sealed registry, the method's generated subset, and the emitted variant, all present at the Exec request surface. Q2: Core owns the closed registry and per-method admissibility. Q3: E0 is where the Exec-branch rejection is authored and returned; the exec branch never reaches L1, so no live-station filing may claim it. Q4: adapter-added variants and driver-decoded native codes are filed on their own traversals. `unrepresentable`.
entries.traversal: One Exec or Process-control request inside an existing Sandbox, rejected at E0
entries.remediation: Emit an admitted registry variant for this method; never introduce a Process-control-specific open reason string.

entries.title: Creation rejection payload outside its closed schema
entries.statement: Every creation rejection payload is exactly the emitted variant's closed schema and contains no stack trace, secret or credential, host path, raw provider payload, unbounded native metadata, protected resource existence, unredacted command environment, or arbitrary detail map.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the emitted variant's declared payload schema, its disclosure class, and the values being placed in it; all are available where the creation response is composed. Q2: Core owns the variant registry, payload schemas, and disclosure classes. Q3: C0 is where the response is emitted, the last point at which withholding is still correct. Q4: bounding and redacting native evidence before it reaches this point is the driver's obligation and is filed at D0. `reject-at-boundary` because the schema and the candidate values are both in hand; a bounded opaque evidence identifier is the licensed alternative.
entries.traversal: CreateSandbox request ingress and rejection at C0
entries.remediation: Emit only the variant's declared payload fields and link protected context through a bounded opaque evidence identifier.

entries.title: Live rejection payload outside its closed schema
entries.statement: Every live-operation rejection payload is exactly the emitted variant's closed schema and contains no stack trace, secret or credential, host path, raw provider payload, unbounded native metadata, protected resource existence, unredacted command environment, or arbitrary detail map.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the emitted variant's payload schema and disclosure class together with the values being placed in it, all present where the live response is composed. Q2: Core owns the registry, schemas, and disclosure classes. Q3: L0 is the emission station. Q4: driver-side redaction and size bounding are filed at D0 on the runtime traversal. Filed per surface because a single filing would bind creation and Exec encoders to a station they do not traverse. `reject-at-boundary`.
entries.traversal: One live operation against an existing Sandbox, rejected at L0
entries.remediation: Populate only the variant's declared fields; move protected context into the operator-visible evidence record behind an opaque identifier.

entries.title: Exec rejection payload outside its closed schema
entries.statement: Every Exec or Process-control rejection payload is exactly the emitted variant's closed schema and contains no stack trace, secret or credential, host path, raw provider payload, unbounded native metadata, protected resource existence, unredacted command environment, or arbitrary detail map.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the variant's payload schema and disclosure class plus the candidate values, all present where the Exec response is composed; the unredacted command environment risk is specific to this surface. Q2: Core owns the registry, schemas, and disclosure classes. Q3: E0 is the emission station on the exec branch. Q4: provider-evidence bounding is the driver's obligation at D0. `reject-at-boundary`.
entries.traversal: One Exec or Process-control request inside an existing Sandbox, rejected at E0
entries.remediation: Emit only the declared payload fields and never echo argv, environment, or native command output into the public detail.

entries.title: Creation validation or existence disclosure before authorization
entries.statement: A creation request performs only the parsing needed to route and authenticate before authorization at a disclosure-safe scope, and an unauthorized request naming an existing creation target and an authorized request naming an absent one produce observationally equivalent public responses.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the ordered admission sequence declared for this method, the caller's authorization at the parent scope, and the target's existence; all are available at the creation ingress. Q2: Core owns ordered admission and disclosure classes. Q3: C0 is where the response is chosen, the last station at which an existence leak can still be prevented. Q4: the authorization decision itself is not another operation's traversal. `reject-at-boundary`: the ordering and the equivalence are decided from the request, the authorization result, and Core records.
entries.traversal: CreateSandbox request ingress and rejection at C0
entries.remediation: Authorize at a non-leaking scope first, then validate; return the same public response for unauthorized-existing and authorized-absent targets.

entries.title: Live validation or existence disclosure before authorization
entries.statement: A live request performs only the parsing needed to route and authenticate before authorization at a disclosure-safe operation and parent scope, and an unauthorized request against an existing target and an authorized request against an absent target produce observationally equivalent public responses.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are this method's declared ordered admission sequence, the caller's authorization scope, and the target's existence; complete at the live request surface. Q2: Core owns ordered admission and disclosure classes. Q3: L0 is where the public response is chosen. Q4: the authorization decision belongs to this traversal. Filed per surface because a single filing would assert that creation and Exec admission components revalidate a station they do not traverse. `reject-at-boundary`.
