entries.traversal: One live operation against an existing Sandbox, rejected at L0
entries.remediation: Run authorization before semantic validation and keep `PermissionDenied` and `TargetNotFound` observationally equivalent for unauthorized callers.

entries.title: Exec validation or existence disclosure before authorization
entries.statement: An Exec or Process-control request performs only the parsing needed to route and authenticate before authorization at a disclosure-safe operation and parent scope, and an unauthorized request against an existing Sandbox or Process and an authorized request against an absent one produce observationally equivalent public responses.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the declared ordered admission sequence, the caller's authorization scope, and the existence of the Sandbox and Process; all present at the Exec request surface. Q2: Core owns ordered admission and disclosure classes. Q3: E0 is where the exec-branch response is chosen. Q4: the authorization decision belongs to this traversal. `reject-at-boundary`.
entries.traversal: One Exec or Process-control request inside an existing Sandbox, rejected at E0
entries.remediation: Authorize before resolving Process existence, and return the same public response whether the Process is absent or merely invisible to this caller.

entries.title: Creation recovery expressed outside the closed recovery contract
entries.statement: Every creation rejection carries exactly one closed `CallerRecovery` consistent with its variant's semantic domain, and no boolean retryability flag substitutes for it and no `after` or `Retry-After` hint independently authorizes replay of an effect.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the emitted variant, its registered `CallerRecovery`, and any timing hint attached to the response; all present where the creation response is composed. Q2: Core owns the recovery vocabulary and the per-variant binding. Q3: C0 is the emission station. Q4: an adapter that rewrites recovery advice commits that at the framework traversal. `reject-at-boundary` because the contradiction is visible between the variant and the emitted recovery.
entries.traversal: CreateSandbox request ingress and rejection at C0
entries.remediation: Emit the variant's registered `CallerRecovery`; treat `Retry-After` only as timing for an already-permitted action.

entries.title: Live recovery expressed outside the closed recovery contract
entries.statement: Every live-operation rejection carries exactly one closed `CallerRecovery` consistent with its variant's semantic domain, and no boolean retryability flag substitutes for it and no `after` or `Retry-After` hint independently authorizes replay of an effect.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the emitted variant, its registered recovery instruction, and any timing hint; complete where the live response is composed. Q2: Core owns the recovery vocabulary. Q3: L0 is the emission station. Q4: adapter rewriting is filed on the framework traversal. This surface carries the sharpest witness: a `RecoveryError` must project `ObserveHandle` or `OperatorAction` and never authorize resubmission under a new key. `reject-at-boundary`.
entries.traversal: One live operation against an existing Sandbox, rejected at L0
entries.remediation: Bind each variant to its single registered recovery action; never emit a retryable boolean or let a wait hint imply replay permission.

entries.title: Exec recovery expressed outside the closed recovery contract
entries.statement: Every Exec or Process-control rejection carries exactly one closed `CallerRecovery` consistent with its variant's semantic domain, and no boolean retryability flag substitutes for it and no `after` or `Retry-After` hint independently authorizes replay of a command or a replacement execution.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the emitted variant, its registered recovery instruction, and any timing hint, all present at the Exec response boundary; the exec-specific risk is advising a new sequence or a replacement execution. Q2: Core owns the recovery vocabulary and the Process-control replay rules. Q3: E0 is the emission station on the exec branch. Q4: adapter auto-replay is a framework-owned violation filed on its own traversal. `reject-at-boundary`.
entries.traversal: One Exec or Process-control request inside an existing Sandbox, rejected at E0
entries.remediation: Emit the registered recovery action; an expired Process-control coordinate recovers by observation or operator action, never by a new sequence.

entries.title: Transport status treated as creation semantics
entries.statement: Canonical HTTP and gRPC status for a creation call is generated from the Core-authored variant and never the reverse, so a transport-local failure never becomes a Core rejection or Core outcome and an accepted result is delivered embedded in its durable handle under a successful transport status even when its terminal outcome is `failed`, `cancelled`, or `unknown`.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the Core-authored semantic result and the transport status being applied to it; both exist where the creation response is emitted. Q2: Core owns the semantic result and the generated projection table. Q3: C0 is the emission station and the last point at which a projection inversion can be refused. Q4: an SDK that reinterprets its own local transport failure commits that outside Core and is filed on the framework traversal. `reject-at-boundary`: the projection is a table lookup over facts already held.
entries.traversal: CreateSandbox request ingress and response emission at C0
entries.remediation: Derive the status from the product variant; return accepted work as its durable Operation with a successful transport status.

entries.title: Transport status treated as live-operation semantics
entries.statement: Canonical HTTP and gRPC status for a live call is generated from the Core-authored variant and never the reverse, so transport `UNKNOWN`, `CANCELLED`, `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, or `UNAVAILABLE` never becomes the corresponding Operation outcome and retrieving an accepted handle whose terminal outcome is `failed`, `cancelled`, or `unknown` is a successful observation.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the Core-authored semantic result and the transport status applied to it; complete at the live response boundary. Q2: Core owns terminal outcomes and the generated projection table. Q3: L0 is where the live response and handle retrieval are emitted. Q4: whether the outcome itself is legal is a separate outcome-proof rule filed at the terminalization station. Filed per surface because a single filing would bind creation and Exec encoders to a station they never traverse. `reject-at-boundary`.
entries.traversal: One live operation or handle retrieval against an existing Sandbox, at L0
entries.remediation: Return the Operation resource with its embedded terminal outcome under a successful status; never map a transport code onto an Operation outcome.

entries.title: Transport status treated as Exec semantics
entries.statement: Canonical HTTP and gRPC status for an Exec or Process-control call is generated from the Core-authored variant and never the reverse, so a transport failure never becomes a Core rejection, a Process termination, or a control-command outcome, and an accepted Process or receipt is returned under a successful transport status regardless of its embedded terminal outcome.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the Core-authored semantic result and the transport status applied to it, both present at the Exec response boundary; the exec-specific risk is a closed connection or client timeout being read as a Process outcome while the process continues. Q2: Core owns the Process record, the receipt, and the projection table. Q3: E0 is the emission station on the exec branch. Q4: decoding native evidence into a termination arm is the driver's obligation on the runtime traversal. `reject-at-boundary`.
entries.traversal: One Exec or Process-control request inside an existing Sandbox, at E0
entries.remediation: Return the durable Process or receipt under a successful status; never convert a closed connection or client deadline into a Process termination.

entries.title: Unrecognized native code extending the public union
entries.statement: An unrecognized native provider code, status, or future provider state is retained as protected evidence and mapped conservatively onto an already-registered public variant, and never adds, widens, parameterizes, or passes through a public variant at runtime.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the decoded native code, the driver's declared decoding version, and the registered public union; all are complete at the driver/provider decoding boundary. Q2: the driver/provider boundary owns trusted decoding of native evidence. Q3: D0 is the decoding station and the last point at which an unmapped code can be refused before it reaches any Core record or public response. Q4: emitting a non-registry variant on a request surface is the Core-owned rule filed at that surface. `reject-at-boundary`, with the legalized defensive hooks at the later stations.
entries.traversal: Driver decoding of provider evidence at the runtime boundary, D0
entries.remediation: Map the unrecognized code conservatively onto a registered variant and record the native code only in the protected evidence record.

entries.title: Raw provider evidence escaping redaction or size bounds
entries.statement: Decoded provider and driver evidence reaches a public response only as the emitted variant's declared payload plus a bounded opaque evidence identifier, and raw native payloads, unbounded metadata, and unredacted values remain confined to the protected evidence record.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the native payload, its size and redaction state, and the declared public projection of the decoding adapter; all are complete at the decoding boundary. Q2: the driver/provider boundary owns evidence decoding, redaction, and bounding. Q3: D0 is the last station at which unbounded or unredacted native material can be withheld before it can be copied into any Core record or response. Q4: what the request surface is permitted to emit is the Core-owned payload rule filed at that surface. `reject-at-boundary`.
entries.traversal: Driver decoding of provider evidence at the runtime boundary, D0
entries.remediation: Store the bounded redacted payload and digest in the protected evidence record and expose only its opaque identifier publicly.

entries.title: Create request omits its resolved initial runtime selection
entries.statement: Every accepted CreateSandbox request and its Operation record carry the resolved `initialRuntime` value drawn from the closed `running`/`stopped` vocabulary, with no CLI, SDK, named-profile, schema, or provider default applied after acceptance or left invisible in the canonical request.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Create request schema and the canonical request it produces, complete at creation-request resolution. Q2: L1.D2 argued `core` and L3.D7 argued `create`; resolved to `create` under Criterion O, because the invalid state is an expressible request whose `initialRuntime` is absent, decided from the Create request schema. Q3: C0 is the last station at which refusing still prevents an invisible default from binding. Q4: the offending act is the Create itself. Merged with index 129 (L0.D5, L1.D2, L2.D7, L3.D7). Index 97 (initially stopped creation performs launch effects) remains the second, genuinely distinct TAXONOMY-04 filing.
entries.traversal: CreateSandbox launch traversal, at creation-request resolution
entries.remediation: Resolve `running` or `stopped` in the caller or profile layer and submit the exact value in the canonical request.

entries.title: Initially stopped creation performs launch effects
entries.statement: A creation whose resolved `initialRuntime` is `stopped` commits a durable Sandbox whose runtime state is `stopped` and never enters `provisioning` or performs a launch effect.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the resolved initial-runtime selection and the Sandbox record being committed, both complete at C0; the driver, host, and provider are never consulted for a creation that must not launch. Q2: the durable creation commit and the dispatch of a launch effect are the control plane's own artefacts. Q3: C0, because the resolved creation is handed to operator placement and host preflight immediately after, and a stopped creation that reaches those stations has already begun the launch it must not perform. Q4: this same creation commits the violation. `reject-at-boundary` because the creation boundary holds every fact needed to refuse.
entries.traversal: CreateSandbox traversal for `initialRuntime = stopped`, at creation commit
entries.remediation: Commit the stopped Sandbox record without launch and require an explicit StartSandbox to establish a runtime.

entries.title: Caller writes Sandbox runtime, desired state, or a presentation label
entries.statement: Sandbox `status` -- its `runtime`, `execution`, `lifecycleOperation`, and `conditions` members -- is an output-only projection: no public request type carries a runtime state, a caller-writable desired runtime state, or a verb-derived presentation label as input, so every lifecycle change is an explicit named command and never a reconciled declaration.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the declared shape of the public live request types and the Sandbox `status` projection, both complete at semantic decoding. Q2: owner was contested between `live` and `core` and is resolved to `live` by Criterion O -- the invalid state is an expressible request at its own caller station. Q3: L0 is the decoding station and the only point at which the input can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the caller's own request. Merged with index 127 (L0.D6, L1.D1, L2.D6, L3.D7 ref). This entry carries the request-input clause of LIFECYCLE-03; the storage/serialization-oracle clause is carried by the M11 survivor at L1, its own station -- the clause partition L0.D7 and L1.D19 asked for.
entries.traversal: any live Sandbox request, at semantic decoding
entries.remediation: Issue the named lifecycle operation that produces the wanted state and read status as an observation, or declare desired state in a Managed-Sandbox Service that issues the same Core operations.

entries.title: Expiry creates a redundant Stop against a proven stopped Sandbox
entries.statement: A durable expiration trigger creates a system-originated `StopSandbox` Operation only when an extant runtime remains, and creates none when the Sandbox already carries a current durable stopped proof.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the durably recorded expiry trigger and the Sandbox's current durable stopped proof, both Core records complete at the lifecycle admission station L0. Q2: the expiry trigger and the stopped proof are Core durable records consulted here, but under Criterion O the invalid state is an expressible Stop admission at its own caller station, so the owner is `live`. Q3: L0, because acceptance durably seizes the lifecycle lane and publishes a stopping projection for a Sandbox already proven stopped. Q4: the offending operation is this system-originated Stop itself, and under the system-origin ruling it is filed at exactly the station its caller-originated twin uses, which is Stop admission at L0. `reject-at-boundary` under Ruling R2: the stopped proof is a Core durable fact, not current external state.
entries.traversal: system-originated StopSandbox from an expiration trigger, at live admission
entries.remediation: Consult the durable stopped proof before creating the expiry Stop and link the existing proof instead.

entries.title: Verb-derived presentation label stored as Sandbox state
entries.statement: Sandbox runtime state is exactly one of `provisioning`, `running`, `suspended`, `stopped`, or `unknown`; every derived presentation label -- creating, starting, suspending, resuming, stopping, restoring, deleting, snapshotting, migrating -- is recomputed at read time from the durable Operation and that authoritative status, and is never independently stored or used as the serialization oracle.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the durable Operation kind and the authoritative Core runtime status at the Operation and status commit station. Q2: the protected artefact is the Core durable status record and its serialization oracle, so the owner is `core`. Q3: L1 is the commit station at which a stored presentation label would first become durable. Q4: the offending act is the lifecycle mutation's own commit. Merged from indices 101 and 128 (L0.D7, L1.D19, L2.D11). This entry carries only the storage/oracle clause of LIFECYCLE-03; the request-input clause is at the M2 survivor at L0, its own station.
entries.traversal: any live lifecycle-mutation traversal, at Operation and status commit
entries.remediation: Derive presentation words at read time from the Operation kind and the authoritative status, and store neither.

entries.title: Execution admission accepting without a proven running epoch
entries.statement: A live operation publishes execution admission `accepting` only for a retained runtime epoch proven present and executing under current fenced authority with runtime state `running`; every other runtime state commits `closed` with a typed reason.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the durable runtime epoch, its proven presence and authority, and the execution-admission projection about to be committed -- all Core durable records at the status commit station. Q2: the protected artefact is the Core status commit, so the owner is `core` under Criterion O. Q3: L1 is the commit station and the last point at which an incorrect `accepting` can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the live lifecycle mutation's own status commit. Merged with index 138 (L0.D10, L1.D4, L2.D4). Index 140 (core, R1->R1, observed-conformance) is retained unchanged as the launch-station sibling -- a legitimate per-station split, not a duplicate.
entries.traversal: any live lifecycle-mutation traversal, at status commit
entries.remediation: Commit `closed` with its typed reason for every runtime state other than `running` for the exact current epoch under current authority.

entries.title: Suspended reported without proven quiescence and continuity
entries.statement: A `SuspendSandbox` Operation succeeds only when workload execution is proven quiesced, no Process can execute, the current runtime epoch and the capability-required memory and Process continuity are proven retained, and execution admission is committed `closed`.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the post-effect quiescence, continuity, and admission evidence for this Suspend, which exist only after the suspend effect has been applied, at the live-mutation resolution station L1. Q2: publishing the terminal outcome and the `suspended` status is a Core durable-record act, so the owner is `core`. Q3: L1, the station at which the Operation terminalizes; refusing later is not a correct implementation because the caller has already been told the Sandbox is suspended. Q4: the same Suspend commits the violation. `observed-conformance` because the predicate is provable only from evidence returned after the effect.
entries.traversal: SuspendSandbox live-mutation traversal, at Operation resolution
entries.remediation: Publish `suspended` only from returned quiescence and same-epoch continuity evidence; otherwise terminalize the Suspend as failed or unresolved.

entries.title: Driver reports Suspend or Resume without same-epoch continuity evidence
entries.statement: A driver reports a successful Suspend or Resume only by returning target-specific evidence that the identical runtime epoch, its retained memory, and its Process continuity survived the transition.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the target's native continuity probes and their decoded results for this transition, which exist only after the driver has performed it, at L1. Q2: producing and decoding native evidence at the driver/provider boundary is owned by `runtime`, which is why this is a separate entry from the Core rule that consumes the evidence. Q3: L1, because the driver's report is what the Core terminalization consumes and there is no later driver station on this traversal. Q4: the driver acts within this same Suspend or Resume. `observed-conformance` because the evidence exists only post-effect.
entries.traversal: SuspendSandbox or ResumeSandbox live-mutation traversal, at driver report
entries.remediation: Return the target's continuity probes with the report, and report failure when the target cannot prove same-epoch retention.

entries.title: Cold fallback reported as a successful Resume
entries.statement: A `ResumeSandbox` Operation succeeds only when post-effect evidence proves the retained runtime epoch resumed under exclusive authority with control and conformance re-proven, and an observed cold fallback, replacement instance, or reconstruction terminates that Resume as failed or unresolved rather than as same-epoch continuation.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the post-effect continuity evidence weighed against the outcome being reported and the retain-versus-allocate epoch decision, complete only at the live-mutation resolution station L1. Q2: the reported terminal outcome and the epoch decision are both Core facts, which resolves the recorded owner disagreement in favour of `core`; the driver's obligation to produce the evidence is the separate `runtime` entry. Q3: L1, because success published there is the false claim itself. Q4: the same Resume commits the violation. `observed-conformance` because continuity is provable only after the resume effect.
entries.traversal: ResumeSandbox live-mutation traversal, at Operation resolution
entries.remediation: Terminalize a Resume that observed a cold fallback as failed or unresolved and leave any replacement to an explicitly authorized Start.

entries.title: Running resize hides reboot, replacement, or partial application
entries.statement: A `ResizeSandboxResources` Operation against a `running` Sandbox succeeds only when evidence proves the complete requested allocation was applied atomically in place with the current epoch retained and without reboot, runtime replacement, or Process identity loss.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the applied-resource evidence, the epoch observed after the effect, and the Process identity set, all of which exist only once the resize has been attempted, at L1. Q2: publishing the terminal outcome and the resulting runtime facts is owned by `core`. Q3: L1, because success published there asserts the postcondition. Q4: the same resize commits the violation. `observed-conformance` because a partial provider update and a hidden replacement are distinguishable only from post-effect evidence.
entries.traversal: ResizeSandboxResources live-mutation traversal against a running Sandbox, at Operation resolution
entries.remediation: Terminalize a partial or replacement-based resize as failed and require an explicit Stop, stopped resize, and Start instead.

entries.title: Stopped resize claims current provider capacity
entries.statement: A `ResizeSandboxResources` Operation against a `stopped` Sandbox commits the validated concrete allocation for the next Start only, allocating no runtime epoch and claiming no current provider capacity.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the validated allocation and the Sandbox's stopped runtime record; the rule is decided from Core records alone with no external probe. Q2: the durable allocation record is owned by `core`. Q3: L1, the commit station for this live mutation, after which the allocation is published as if reserved. Q4: the same resize commits the violation. `reject-at-boundary` rather than `observed-conformance` because no post-effect evidence is required, and rather than `dynamic-preflight` under Ruling R2 because the allocation record is a Core durable fact.
entries.traversal: ResizeSandboxResources live-mutation traversal against a stopped Sandbox, at Operation resolution
entries.remediation: Commit the next-Start allocation and report no epoch, reservation, or current capacity for a stopped Sandbox.

entries.title: Stop lowered to a destructive provider delete
entries.statement: A driver lowering `StopSandbox` uses only native steps that end the current runtime epoch and establish containment absence for it, leaving the logical Sandbox and its retained state intact, and never substitutes a provider delete, destroy, permanent kill, or other destructive removal.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the lowering the driver actually chose for one StopSandbox and the native steps the target exposes, both complete at driver lowering. Q2: the invalid state is an unproven driver claim about how a Core postcondition is realized, so the owner is `runtime` under Criterion O. Q3: L1 is the last station at which refusing still prevents a destructive removal from being dispatched under a Stop. Q4: the offending act is the lowering chosen on the live Stop traversal. Merged with index 139, a verbatim-title duplicate of one underlying problem (L0.D9, L1.D0, L2.D1, L3.D6); the merged content takes ADM's containment-absence framing onto the SBX index so neither statement is lost. Not folded into `142` (runtime, D0->D0, driver postcondition fidelity): under Criterion P the fact sets differ, since `142` reads the driver's declared postcondition contract at the launch-branch driver station while this entry reads the lowering actually chosen for one Stop on the live traversal, which never reaches D0.
entries.traversal: StopSandbox live-mutation traversal, at driver lowering
entries.remediation: Lower Stop to close-admission, revoke-launch, drain, terminate, and prove-absence steps against the current epoch, reject the target profile when only a destructive removal exists, and let the caller issue DeleteSandbox separately.

entries.title: Unprovable runtime state approximated as stopped or running
entries.statement: When runtime presence or absence, claimed-epoch continuity, exclusive effect authority, containment emptiness, or external-effect liveness cannot be safely established, the committed Sandbox runtime state is `unknown` with execution admission `closed`.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the evidence set gathered for this lifecycle mutation weighed against the five presence, continuity, authority, containment, and liveness predicates, complete only at the resolution station L1. Q2: the published runtime state is a Core durable record, so the owner is `core`. Q3: L1, because the approximation becomes authoritative the moment it is committed and would then admit Exec or successor authority. Q4: the same lifecycle mutation commits the approximation. `observed-conformance` because insufficiency of proof is established only from post-effect evidence.
entries.traversal: any live lifecycle-mutation traversal, at status commit
entries.remediation: Commit `unknown` with closed admission and retain the evidence for a system-originated reconciliation Operation.

entries.title: Provider or adapter phase mapped to Core runtime state
entries.statement: A decoded provider, host, or VMM lifecycle phase, status enum, or handle state is retained as non-authoritative evidence and is never mapped by name onto a Core Sandbox runtime state.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the decoded provider vocabulary and the closed Core runtime-state vocabulary, both complete at the driver decoding boundary D0 with no further observation required. Q2: decoding provider vocabulary is the driver/provider boundary, so the owner is `runtime`. Q3: D0, because a name-mapped state leaving the decoding boundary is indistinguishable from proven Core truth at every later station. Q4: the mapping is committed by the driver on the traversal being described. This entry reads the provider's phase vocabulary; the separate fencing entry reads the provider event's claimed epoch, which is a different fact set.
entries.traversal: driver decoding of provider state on any traversal entering the driver boundary
entries.remediation: Record the provider phase as evidence and derive Core runtime state only from the postcondition proofs the Core contract requires.

entries.title: Provider-native TTL, auto-stop, or auto-delete left enabled
entries.statement: Generated target configuration disables every provider-native TTL, idle-sleep, auto-stop, and auto-delete mechanism, or fences it behind the Core durable expiry sequence.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the target's native expiry knobs and the total generated configuration derived from PreparedLaunch, complete at D0 where that configuration is derived and validated. Q2: generated backend configuration is the driver boundary, so the owner is `runtime`. Q3: D0, because the configuration is dispatched immediately afterwards and a native timer left enabled thereafter can end the runtime with no Core Operation. Q4: the launch traversal being described is the one that emits the configuration.
entries.traversal: launch traversal, at generated target-configuration derivation
entries.remediation: Emit explicit disabling values for every native expiry knob, or bind them to the Core expiry sequence and record the fence.

entries.title: Launch succeeds before control, conformance, and admission are proven
entries.statement: A Create-running, Start, or same-Sandbox Restore Operation succeeds only when the new runtime epoch is observed present and executing and its declared control, conformance, and `accepting` execution-admission postconditions are each proven.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the launch evidence set for the exact new epoch, including the control-attachment, conformance, and admission probe results, which exist only at the launch resolution station R1. Q2: publishing an Operation as `succeeded` is a terminal-outcome act, which resolves the recorded owner disagreement in favour of `core`. Q3: R1, the last station on the launch traversal at which withholding success is correct. Q4: the launch this entry describes commits the violation; the rule is filed as an R1 self-pair rather than the forbidden C0-to-R1 pair, because resolution-stage components do not revalidate a launch postcondition. `observed-conformance` because the postcondition is provable only after launch.
entries.traversal: launch traversal for CreateSandbox running, StartSandbox, or same-Sandbox Restore, at launch resolution
entries.remediation: Publish launch success only after all declared control, conformance, and admission probes pass for the exact new epoch.

entries.title: Driver claims launch success without its declared probes
entries.statement: A launch driver reports success only after executing its declared control-attachment, conformance, and execution-admission probes against the exact new runtime epoch and returning their evidence.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the driver's declared probe set and the native results it obtained for this epoch, available only after launch at R1. Q2: executing and decoding the probes is the driver/provider boundary, so the owner is `runtime`; this is the supply side of the Core rule that consumes the evidence and is a separate entry because the fact sets and owners differ. Q3: R1, because the Core terminalization immediately consumes the driver's report. Q4: the driver acts within this same launch traversal.
entries.traversal: launch traversal, at driver launch report
entries.remediation: Run every declared probe for the new epoch and report failure when any probe is unavailable or unproven.

entries.title: Provider acknowledgement treated as the required Core postcondition
entries.statement: Backend acceptance checkpoints such as OCI `created`, containerd task registration, VMM configuration, guest-agent handshake, or provider request acknowledgement are decoded evidence only, and each Core postcondition is proven by the evidence its own contract names.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the decoded provider evidence weighed against the Core proof obligation at the trusted-probe station, available only after the launch attempt at R1. Q2: deciding which native evidence discharges which obligation at report time is the driver/provider boundary, so the owner is `runtime`. Q3: R1, because the report is consumed by Core terminalization there. Q4: the driver acts within this launch traversal. The driver's separately declared evidence contract, complete at D0, is a distinct fencing entry and is not merged here.
entries.traversal: launch traversal, at driver evidence report
entries.remediation: Keep provider acknowledgements as evidence and satisfy each postcondition with the exact proof its contract requires.

entries.title: Provider-driven expiry relabeled a successful Core Stop or Delete
entries.statement: An unpreventable provider expiry, idle stop, or reclamation is recorded as an uncontrolled provider-loss event requiring reconciliation, never retrospectively as a successful Core Stop or Delete.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the observed provider-initiated termination and the absence of a Core Operation whose postcondition it could discharge, available only once the loss is observed on the reconciliation traversal at R1. Q2: classifying the event and writing the durable outcome are Core acts, so the owner is `core`. Q3: R1, the station at which the reconciliation Operation terminalizes; relabelling committed there is the false claim. Q4: the reconciliation traversal that observes the loss is the one described, and under the system-origin ruling it is filed at its caller-originated twin's station. `observed-conformance` because the classification rests on post-launch observation.
entries.traversal: system-originated reconciliation traversal after an observed provider expiry, at Operation resolution
entries.remediation: Record the provider loss as its own event and reconcile the runtime state instead of crediting a Core Stop or Delete.

entries.title: Provider auto-wake runtime left unsequenced
entries.statement: A provider-created replacement runtime observed without a Core lifecycle request is durably sequenced as a new runtime epoch with its identity and execution-admission records committed.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the observed replacement runtime, its proven discontinuity from the prior epoch, and the Core identity and admission records that must precede acceptance, all available only after the wake is observed on the reconciliation traversal at R1. Q2: epoch sequencing and admission are Core durable records, so the owner is `core`. Q3: R1, the last station at which the Core can refuse to open admission; after admission opens, a Process is already bound to an unsequenced runtime. Q4: the reconciliation traversal that observes the wake is the one described, and a later Exec against the unsequenced epoch is filed on its own traversal. `observed-conformance` because the replacement is provable only from post-launch observation.
entries.traversal: system-originated reconciliation traversal after an observed provider auto-wake, at Operation resolution
entries.remediation: Sequence the observed runtime as a new epoch and open execution admission only after that record is durable.

entries.title: Stopped published without a containment-absence proof
entries.statement: A driver publishes `stopped` only after proving its containment-specific absence boundary, such as cgroup emptiness for process targets or host VMM absence for VM targets, and never from a guest shutdown acknowledgement, power-down request, provider stop acknowledgement, or initial-child exit.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the target's containment-absence evidence and the weaker acknowledgements that must not substitute for it, available only once teardown has been attempted, at T0. Q2: producing the containment-specific proof is the driver/provider boundary, so the owner is `runtime`. Q3: T0 is a sink and the last station on this traversal at which withholding the `stopped` publication is correct. Q4: the Stop traversal being described commits the violation; the source-stopped Snapshot obligation reads the same information set at the same station and is carried here as a required witness rather than as a second entry.
entries.traversal: StopSandbox teardown traversal, at containment-absence proof
entries.remediation: Prove containment emptiness with the target's own kernel or host evidence before publishing `stopped`.

entries.title: Stop grace deadline treated as an absence proof
entries.statement: A Stop that cannot prove containment absence commits Sandbox runtime state `unknown` and retains its evidence, and the grace deadline alone never establishes absence.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the driver's absence proof or its absence together with the elapsed grace deadline, complete only at the teardown station T0. Q2: committing the resulting runtime state is a Core durable-record act, distinct from the driver's obligation to produce the proof, so the owner is `core` and this is a separate entry from the driver-side rule. Q3: T0, a sink and the last correct refusal point. Q4: the same Stop traversal commits the state. `observed-conformance` because insufficiency of the absence proof is established only from post-effect evidence.
entries.traversal: StopSandbox teardown traversal, at runtime-state commit
entries.remediation: Commit `unknown` and preserve the evidence when the grace deadline expires without a containment-absence proof.

entries.title: Delete succeeds with incomplete cleanup or a possibly live orphan
entries.statement: A `DeleteSandbox` Operation succeeds only when the live Sandbox aggregate and every Core-owned live resource covered by that Operation are proven absent and the cleanup proof is durable.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the cleanup evidence for every covered resource and the proof that no orphan retains effect authority, available only once deletion has been attempted, at T0. Q2: publishing the terminal outcome and the tombstone is a Core durable-record act, so the owner is `core`. Q3: T0, a sink and the last station at which withholding success is correct. Q4: the Delete traversal being described commits the violation; the independent retention of Operation, Process, output, and evidence records is a different fact set filed in the retention family.
entries.traversal: DeleteSandbox teardown traversal, at Operation resolution
entries.remediation: Terminalize an incompletely proven deletion as failed or unresolved, retain the cleanup obligation, and never claim success with cleanup pending.

entries.title: Incompatible concurrent lifecycle mutations both receive authority
entries.statement: At most one nonterminal Operation holds the fenced Sandbox lifecycle-mutation lane, and a request whose ordered operation pair with the lane holder is not an explicitly permitted row of the compatibility ledger is refused with the typed conflict naming that active Operation.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the durable lane record, the incoming request's kind and target, and the reviewed compatibility row for that ordered pair, all complete at the live admission station L0 with no external probe. Q2: the lane record and Operation acceptance are Core durable facts, so the owner is `core`. Q3: L0 is the last station at which refusal is correct, because acceptance durably grants the lane and both mutations then hold authority; the loser of the Resume-versus-Stop race is decided by which request durably acquires the lane here. Q4: the offending operation is the second request itself, whose own admission this entry describes. `reject-at-boundary` under Ruling R2 because lane occupancy is a Core durable record. Ledger totality — that no pair row may be absent and none may inherit from a provider verb — has no traversal answer to the first two questions and is carried as a ledger validator rule, not duplicated here.
entries.traversal: second concurrent lifecycle-mutation request, at live admission
entries.remediation: Wait for or cancel the active lifecycle Operation, or issue a pair the compatibility ledger explicitly permits.

entries.title: Unsupported capability approximated at creation
entries.statement: A creation requiring a capability-gated Core behavior resolves a target profile advertising that exact conformed capability, and an unadvertised capability is rejected rather than approximated by a different mechanism, a weaker guarantee, or a provider default.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the creation's required capability set and the effective capabilities of the resolved member and runtime profile, which first exist together where the verified manifest and the CreateSandbox input meet at C0; no host or provider state is consulted, since capability advertisement is an immutable resolved fact. Q2: the creation request surface owns the resolution, so the owner is `create`. Q3: C0, the last station at which refusal is correct, because the resolved creation passes to operator placement and driver preparation immediately afterwards and an approximation made there is invisible to the caller. Q4: the same creation commits the violation; the live-request half of this obligation is a different owner and station and is carried by the existing live capability entry.
entries.traversal: CreateSandbox traversal, at creation resolution
entries.remediation: Select a profile advertising the exact conformed capability, or drop the capability-gated requirement from the creation.

entries.title: Expiration removal widens a policy-owned lifecycle bound
entries.statement: `SetSandboxExpiration` assigns or removes only the caller-managed schedule, and every Artifact hard ceiling and Managed-Sandbox lifecycle policy in force remains binding after the update.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the requested expiration value, whether an instant with its action or explicit removal, together with the Artifact hard ceilings and the Managed-Sandbox lifecycle policy already resolved onto this Sandbox; all are Core-held representation facts complete at the live admission station L0. Q2: the live request surface owns the update, so the owner is `live`. Q3: L0 is the last correct refusal point, because this operation's postcondition is a committed Core representation returned synchronously and no later station on the traversal reconsiders it. Q4: the same request commits the violation; an assigned instant that exceeds an Artifact hard maximum is the widening instance already carried by the existing live-update entry, so only the removal-and-policy-persistence clause is registered here. `reject-at-boundary` under Ruling R2 because the ceilings and the policy are Core durable facts, not current external state.
entries.traversal: SetSandboxExpiration live traversal, at live admission
entries.remediation: Use `none` only to clear the caller schedule, and keep the Artifact and Managed-Sandbox policy bounds in force in the committed record.

entries.title: Generic, compound, or provider-native verb on the public surface
entries.statement: The public caller-facing Core lifecycle and control union contains only named, typed, resource-oriented methods with one exact declared postcondition each, and admits no generic action, compound convenience verb, archive or migration verb, or provider-native verb.
entries.rationale: Q1: deciding this needs only the closed public method union and the submitted request's method identity; both are complete at the live request surface and no later runtime, driver, or provider fact refines the answer. Q2: the public method union is a Core Sandbox API control-plane fact, but under Criterion O the invalid state is an expressible request at its own caller station, so the owner is `live`. Q3: the live request surface is the last station on this traversal at which refusing is correct, because admitting the method commits an acceptance record. Q4: the violation is committed by the same request whose traversal this describes. Disposition is unrepresentable because a closed generated method union gives InvokeAction, RestartSandbox, WakeSandbox, KillSandbox, DestroySandbox, RollbackSandbox, ArchiveSandbox, and a native provider verb no construction path on any supported API. Handoff: system- or operator-originated migration is not a public verb and is filed at `191`.
entries.traversal: one live request against an existing Sandbox, at method identity resolution
entries.remediation: Issue the exact named operations — observe StopSandbox then StartSandbox, SignalProcess, TerminateProcess, StopSandbox then DeleteSandbox, or RestoreSandbox — instead of a generic, compound, or provider-native verb.

entries.title: Public method admitted without one exact target-independent postcondition
entries.statement: Every admitted public method declares one exact target-independent success postcondition that capability gating narrows availability of but no target profile, driver, or provider may reinterpret.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the method's declared success postcondition and the request's method identity, both complete at the live request surface; a name whose meaning depends on which target serves it cannot be decided anywhere later without guessing the target. Q2: the declared success postcondition per method is a Core control-plane fact, but under Criterion O the invalid state is an expressible request at its own caller station, so the owner is `live`. Q3: the live request surface must refuse before an acceptance record binds a meaning the Core cannot state. Q4: same traversal as the request. Unrepresentable because a generated contract requires a successPredicate per method, so a method with no exact postcondition has no construction path.
entries.traversal: one live request against an existing Sandbox, at method identity resolution
entries.remediation: Give the method one exact target-independent postcondition or decompose it into the precise operations whose postconditions the Core can state.

entries.title: Generic Sandbox update method
entries.statement: Sandbox representation changes use only the two narrow etag-guarded operations UpdateSandboxMetadata and SetSandboxExpiration, and no generic update method spans metadata, expiration, resources, network policy, runtime replacement, and provider tier under one contract.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the closed method union plus the substantive fact that those six subjects have different authorization, capability, epoch, and failure contracts; both are complete at the live request surface. Q2: the method union and its per-subject contracts are Core control-plane facts, but under Criterion O the invalid state is an expressible request at its own caller station, so the owner is `live`. Q3: the live request surface is the last correct refusal point, since acceptance would bind one contract to six subjects. Q4: same traversal. This stays separate from the general public-surface entry because it consults the differing per-subject contracts, not only the union membership. Unrepresentable because the generated union has no UpdateSandbox arm.
entries.traversal: one live request against an existing Sandbox, at method identity resolution
entries.remediation: Use UpdateSandboxMetadata or SetSandboxExpiration for representation changes and the exact lifecycle or resize operation for everything else.

entries.title: Attach, connect, detach, shell, or session as a Core method
entries.statement: Attachment, connection, shell, and Session ergonomics remain adapter-owned helpers composed from Sandbox reads, Exec, Process I/O, and the named lifecycle methods, and never become Core methods holding independent lifecycle authority.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the closed public method union and the request's method identity, complete at the live request surface. Q2: which names carry Core lifecycle authority is a Core control-plane fact, but under Criterion O the invalid state is an expressible request at its own caller station, so the owner is `live`. Q3: the live request surface must refuse before an acceptance record grants a client-ergonomic name lifecycle authority. Q4: the adapter-side obligation to own Session rebinding explicitly is a different owner on a different traversal and is filed on the adapter boundary, not here. Unrepresentable because these names have no arm in the generated Core method union.
entries.traversal: one live request against an existing Sandbox, at method identity resolution
entries.remediation: Express the intent as Sandbox reads, Exec, Process I/O, and explicit lifecycle methods, and keep attachment or Session state in the adapter.

entries.title: Delete accepted against a Sandbox without a durable stopped proof
entries.statement: `DeleteSandbox` is admitted only against a Sandbox holding a current durable stopped proof and never performs a silent compound stop-then-delete; a system-originated expiry Delete is created at exactly the same station under the same proof and is linked to the Stop Operation whose outcome established it.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Delete request and the Sandbox's current durable stopped proof, both complete at live admission. Q2: owner was contested between `core` and `live` and resolves to `live` under Criterion O -- the invalid state is an admitted Delete request. Q3: L0 is the last station at which refusing still prevents a silent compound stop-then-delete. Q4: the offending act is the Delete request, caller- or expiry-originated. Merged from indices 100 and 130 (L1.D3): one rule split on `origin`, which the binding ruling forbids as an information set. `operation.origin` therefore appears as a diagnostic path only, never as an information set.
entries.traversal: one DeleteSandbox request against an existing Sandbox, caller- or expiry-originated
entries.remediation: Issue and observe StopSandbox first, then issue DeleteSandbox against the proven stopped Sandbox; an expiry Delete is created only from a durable stopped proof and links the Stop Operation that produced it.

entries.title: Restore accepted against a non-stopped Sandbox
entries.statement: Same-Sandbox RestoreSandbox is admitted only against a stopped Sandbox and only with a Snapshot proven complete and compatible with that Sandbox's pinned Artifact, member, and runtime-profile identity.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the request, the Sandbox's current durable runtime state, and the Snapshot manifest's completeness and pinned identities — all in the live request surface's information set. Q2: admission of one operation against an existing Sandbox is the live request surface. Q3: the live surface is the last correct refusal point, because acceptance allocates a new runtime epoch before restore effects. Q4: the epoch allocation itself and the no-reactivation postcondition are different fact sets on the Core and launch traversals and are filed there. Reject-at-boundary under Ruling R2: the runtime state and Snapshot manifest are Core durable records.
entries.traversal: one RestoreSandbox request against an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Stop the Sandbox and observe its durable stopped proof, then restore from a complete Snapshot pinned to the same Artifact, member, and runtime profile.

entries.title: Representation update changes runtime authority, epoch, or policy
entries.statement: An accepted `UpdateSandboxMetadata` or `SetSandboxExpiration` commits only the Core-owned representation record and its revision, leaving the runtime epoch, mutation authority, resolved Artifact policy, and running workload unchanged.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the submitted representation update and the Core representation record it targets, both complete at live admission. Q2: the invalid state is an admitted live request against an existing Sandbox, so the owner is `live`. Q3: L0 is the last station at which refusing still prevents a representation update from touching runtime authority. Q4: the offending act is the caller's update request. Merged with index 25 (L0.D11, L1.D18, L2.D5). The immutable-name clause is removed from this statement: entry 24 (IDE, live, L0->L0, unrepresentable -- no update request can express a replacement name) is the sole authority for it, which clears L1.D18's disposition collision so one field can no longer be both unconstructible and boundary-rejected.
entries.traversal: one atomic Core-record update against an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Restrict metadata and expiration updates to labels, correlation metadata, and the caller-managed expiration schedule, and use the exact lifecycle or resize operation for anything else.

entries.title: Exec accepted after execution admission closed or an expiry trigger was recorded
entries.statement: An Exec request is admitted only while the bound Sandbox runtime's execution admission is durably accepting, and is refused with its exact typed reason once a lifecycle operation closes admission or an expiration instant is durably recorded as a system trigger.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the durable execution-admission state and its reason together with the Exec request's bound Sandbox runtime reference; both are complete at the Exec request station. Q2: one Process request inside an existing Sandbox is the exec request surface. Q3: the Exec request station is the last correct refusal point, because the next act on this traversal is the durable Process acceptance commit that Stop's captured set must not contain. Q4: the lifecycle operation's obligation to close admission before capturing its Process set is a different owner on the live traversal and is filed there. Reject-at-boundary under Ruling R2: admission state is a Core durable record.
entries.traversal: one Exec request inside an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Observe execution admission before submitting Exec, and after a lifecycle operation or expiry trigger start a new runtime epoch before executing again.

entries.title: Exec accepted against a provider-created epoch before Core sequences it
entries.statement: An Exec is admitted against a runtime that a provider auto-wake, standby recovery, or lazy creation produced only after the Core has durably sequenced that runtime's epoch identity and execution admission.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the Core durable epoch-identity and admission records for the observed runtime against the Exec request's runtime reference; both are complete at the Exec request station and no post-dispatch fact is needed. Q2: one Process request inside an existing Sandbox is the exec request surface; the Core sequencing record is the consulted fact. Q3: the Exec request station is the last correct refusal point, because acceptance would bind a Process permanently to an unsequenced epoch. Q4: the reconciliation that establishes the provider-created runtime is a different operation and is filed on its own traversal. Reject-at-boundary: the sequencing record is Core-durable.
entries.traversal: one Exec request inside an existing Sandbox whose current runtime was provider-originated
entries.remediation: Let the system-originated reconciliation Operation durably sequence the new epoch and reopen admission, then submit Exec against that epoch.

entries.title: Process launch dispatched under a revoked launch authority
entries.statement: A Process launch performs its first external dispatch only while its fenced launch-authority grant revalidates as current against the Core durable record.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision needs the accepted Process record, its effect intent, and the current durable launch-authority grant; those facts are complete from the Exec request station, but the grant can be revoked by a concurrent quiescing operation at any moment before dispatch, so the check must be performed immediately before the external effect. Q2: launch authority is a Core fenced-authority fact. Q3: the dispatch station is the last point on this traversal at which refusing is correct, because after dispatch a workload may already be executing. Q4: the quiescing operation's obligation to revoke authority before capturing its set is a different owner on the live traversal.
entries.traversal: one Exec request inside an existing Sandbox, at first external dispatch
entries.remediation: Revalidate the fenced launch-authority grant immediately before dispatch and terminalize or hold the Process when the grant is no longer current.

entries.title: Process set captured before admission and launch authority close
entries.statement: A quiescing or absence-proving operation durably closes execution admission and revokes new Process launch authority before it snapshots the Process set of the current epoch.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the durable admission-closure record, the launch-authority revocation record, and the captured Process set of the current epoch — all Core facts available at the live operation's effect station. Q2: admission closure, launch authority, and the captured set are Core durable records. Q3: the live operation's own effect station is the last point at which refusing to proceed is correct, because a set captured before closure can be extended by an Exec that the operation will never observe. Q4: the Exec that slips in is refused on its own traversal by the exec-side admission rule; this entry describes the lifecycle operation's ordering obligation. Reject-at-boundary: every consulted fact is a Core durable record.
entries.traversal: one quiescing or absence-proving operation against an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Order the operation as durable admission close, then launch-authority revocation, then Process-set capture, and never capture before both records commit.

entries.title: Withheld launch authority regranted outside a succeeded same-epoch Resume
entries.statement: Launch authority withheld by a continuity-preserving Suspend is regranted only after the same-epoch ResumeSandbox Operation succeeds, while the Process's original deadline remains unexpired and no intervening TerminateProcess request exists.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the Resume Operation's committed outcome, the withheld grant, the Process's original deadline, and any intervening termination request; all four are Core durable records complete at the live operation's effect station. Q2: launch authority, Operation outcomes, and Process deadlines are Core durable records. Q3: the live effect station is the last correct refusal point, because regranting authority permits an external dispatch. Q4: Suspend's obligation to withhold rather than terminalize is a different fact set filed on the Process family. Reject-at-boundary under Ruling R2: no external state is consulted.
entries.traversal: one ResumeSandbox operation against an existing suspended Sandbox
entries.remediation: Regrant launch authority only after the same-epoch Resume Operation commits success, and terminalize the Process when its deadline expired or a termination request intervened.

entries.title: Execution admission accepting on a launch traversal without a proven running epoch
entries.statement: A launch traversal publishes execution admission accepting only for a new runtime epoch proven present and executing under current fenced authority.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the runtime state and execution-admission fields of the status record written at the end of launch, which exist only once launch evidence has been gathered. Q2: the Sandbox status record is a Core durable record. Q3: the launch result station is the last point at which withholding accepting is correct, because publishing it authorizes Exec admission against the new epoch. Q4: the same pairing rule on the live traversal is a separate per-station entry; one combined entry would bind launch components to a live pair they do not traverse. Disposition is observed-conformance because the running fact backing accepting is provable only after launch.
entries.traversal: one launch (Create running, Start, or same-Sandbox Restore) traversal, at status publication
entries.remediation: Prove runtime presence for the new epoch under current authority before publishing execution admission accepting.

entries.title: Unsupported capability approximated by a driver
entries.statement: A driver reports an unsupported capability before any effect-producing work and never approximates it with a different native mechanism.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the validated PreparedLaunch stage's required capability set against the driver's declared conformed capabilities; both are complete at the driver-entry boundary and need no external probe. Q2: declared driver capabilities live at the driver/provider boundary, so runtime owns them. Q3: the driver-entry boundary is the last correct refusal point, because the next act is a native effect. Q4: the caller-facing synchronous rejection of a capability-gated live request is a different owner on the live traversal and is already carried by the existing live-capability entry. Reject-at-boundary: the capability declaration is static driver metadata.
entries.traversal: one driver invocation with a validated PreparedLaunch stage
entries.remediation: Return the typed capability-unsupported result before effect-producing work instead of substituting an approximate native mechanism.

entries.title: Driver widens, narrows, or downgrades the requested postcondition
entries.statement: A driver's native lowering of a Core method establishes exactly the requested postcondition and never a colder, wider, or more destructive fallback.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the requested postcondition carried by the validated PreparedLaunch stage together with the declared postcondition and effect class of each native step; both are complete at the driver-entry boundary. Q2: native step selection at the driver/provider boundary is the runtime owner. Q3: the driver-entry boundary is the last correct refusal point, because the native effect follows immediately. Q4: the public-surface rule that a method must have one exact postcondition is a Core fact set filed separately; this entry constrains the lowering, not the naming. Reject-at-boundary: the declared postcondition of each native step is static driver metadata.
entries.traversal: one driver invocation with a validated PreparedLaunch stage
entries.remediation: Reject the operation as unsupported rather than lowering it to a native step whose postcondition differs from the requested one.

entries.title: Driver advertises Core Exec without full execution conformance
entries.statement: A driver advertises Core Exec only when it proves a targetable execution containment unit covering the Process and its owned descendants, durable output spooling with stable byte cursors and explicit truncation, exact terminal evidence, stdin ownership and close semantics, provable Process termination, and adoption of the same attempted execution after control-plane failure.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the driver's declared conformance evidence for those six requirements; that evidence is static driver metadata complete at the driver-entry boundary and needs no runtime observation. Q2: driver conformance declarations live at the driver/provider boundary. Q3: the driver-entry boundary is the last correct refusal point, because advertising Exec makes the Core admit Exec requests against this target. Q4: the individual Process I/O and termination rules are separate entries on the exec traversal; this entry governs admission of the driver to the Exec surface. Reject-at-boundary: the conformance declaration is available before any effect.
entries.traversal: one driver invocation with a validated PreparedLaunch stage, at capability admission
entries.remediation: Supply a Core-managed in-guest supervisor and durable spool, or do not advertise full Core Exec for this target.

entries.title: Artifact asserts a dynamic Core or runtime fact
entries.statement: An Artifact Definition declares only frontend-independent static facts and cannot express current Sandbox or Process state, current runtime epoch or etag, resource capacity, provider admission, concurrent Operations, Snapshot retention or reference state, expiration races, provider availability, or evidence freshness.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the resolved Artifact Definition's field set against the closed set of declarative facts; that is complete once the Artifact is semantically resolved, and no runtime observation refines it. Q2: Artifact Definition content is owned by artifact. Q3: the build station is the last correct refusal point, because a built manifest that asserts a dynamic fact is thereafter treated as authoritative. Q4: the conformance-evidence instance and the host-path instance extend existing target and Artifact entries and are not refiled here. Unrepresentable because no Artifact schema field can name a current Core or runtime fact.
entries.traversal: Artifact authoring and build traversal
entries.remediation: Express the dynamic condition as a runtime precondition on the Core operation and keep the Artifact limited to declarative facts.

entries.title: Restored or forked runtime admits execution without a successor Process contract
entries.statement: A restored, restore-as-created, or forked runtime admits execution only through a newly allocated durable Core Process carrying its own identity, provenance, deadline, termination-request handling, containment, stdin ownership, durable output cursors, and terminal-evidence contract.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the launched runtime's observed execution units against the Core Process records allocated for the new epoch; those observations exist only after launch. Q2: durable Process identity and its control contract are Core durable records. Q3: the launch result station is the last correct point to refuse success, because publishing the new epoch as usable while an unowned execution acts would leave an uncontrollable workload. Q4: the v1 rejectNonterminal admission rule for capture is a different fact set on the capture request's own traversal. Disposition is observed-conformance because only post-launch observation can show an acting execution without a Core Process.
entries.traversal: one launch traversal following restore, restore-as-create, or fork
entries.remediation: Reject capture while any Core Process is nonterminal, and reintroduce execution in the new epoch through a fresh Exec that allocates a durable Process.

entries.title: Process terminal outcome mutated
entries.statement: A Process terminal outcome is immutable once committed, and every later signal acknowledgement, reaper observation, or provider event arriving after the outcome commit is retained as evidence rather than applied as a rewrite.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the existing terminal Process record and the proposed write; both are Core durable records and the protected outcome first exists at the exec outcome station. Q2: durable Process records and terminal outcomes are Core-owned. Q3: E1 is the exec outcome station and the last point on this traversal at which a late acknowledgement, reaper observation, or provider event can be refused as a rewrite; late evidence arriving during Stop or Delete is refused at `190`. Q4: the protected record is a Process outcome, not an Operation outcome, so this stays separate from the Operation immutability entry on the reconciliation traversal. Reject-at-boundary: refusing the rewrite consults two Core records and needs no new observation.
entries.traversal: one Exec dispatch and its outcome
entries.remediation: Retain the late observation as evidence linked to the Process and leave the committed terminal outcome unchanged.

entries.title: Terminal Operation unknown conflated with reconcilable Process unknown
entries.statement: Process `unknown` is a nonterminal reconcilable observation state drawn from the Process vocabulary, and is never projected as a terminal Operation outcome or treated as replay authorization.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the two closed vocabularies — the Process state graph and the Operation outcome union — together with the record being written; the Process vocabulary is only in scope on a traversal holding a Process record, which is the exec branch. Q2: both vocabularies and the record are Core durable-record facts. Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because the projection is committed there. Q4: filing at the reconciliation station would make launch and reconciliation components assert defensive revalidation of a Process-vocabulary rule they never traverse for exec-originated Processes, which is a false coverage claim; those stations keep only defensive hooks. Reject-at-boundary rather than unrepresentable, because the type-level distinctness of the two unions does not stop a conforming implementation from making this semantic projection error.
entries.traversal: one Exec dispatch and its outcome
entries.remediation: Keep the Process in its reconcilable state and terminalize only the Operation, then resolve the Process through reconciliation of its own launch token.

entries.title: Process-targeted Operation outcome terminalizes the Process
entries.statement: A Signal or Terminate Operation's committed terminal outcome describes only that Operation, and never writes a terminal outcome onto the targeted Process record.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the Process-targeted Operation's committed outcome against the referenced Process record; both are Core durable records complete at the live operation's outcome station. Q2: Operation and Process records are Core-owned. Q3: the live outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because the Operation's terminalization is what tempts the conflation. Q4: the exec-branch conflation of the two vocabularies is a different fact set and is filed on the exec traversal. Reject-at-boundary: two Core records decide it with no new observation.
entries.traversal: one Process-targeted Signal or Terminate operation against an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Terminalize the Operation from its own proof obligations and update the Process only from Process-level termination evidence.

entries.title: Ambiguous Process automatically replaced
entries.statement: An accepted Process whose outcome is unproven is reconciled against its own launch token and is never replaced by a Core- or driver-initiated replacement dispatch.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the accepted Process record, its durable launch token and effect intent, and the current knowledge set for that one attempted execution; all exist at the exec outcome station. Q2: the accepted Process record and its effect intent are Core durable records. Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because the replacement dispatch is the violation. Q4: framing this as an admission gate on a new caller Exec is rejected: it would make a legitimate new command unexpressible while a prior Process is unresolved and destroy the required valid witness, so the rule sits at the outcome station where replacement is chosen; the adapter-side auto-replay prohibition is a different owner filed on the adapter boundary. Reject-at-boundary: the durable intent and knowledge set are Core-held.
entries.traversal: one Exec dispatch and its outcome
entries.remediation: Reconcile the same launch token and, once learned, the same backend execution identity, and leave the Process unproven rather than dispatching a replacement.

entries.title: Termination arm asserted without its exact native evidence
entries.statement: The selected ProcessTermination arm is justified by exactly the native evidence that arm asserts, so a nonzero exit decodes to the exited arm, startFailed proves the command never became running, deadlineExceeded proves the original Process can neither launch nor continue, and lost runtime never decodes to an ordinary exit.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the observed native termination evidence — a wait status, a supervisor execution record, a deadline proof, or a lost-runtime signal — against the closed ProcessTermination union; that evidence exists only once termination is observed. Q2: decoding native evidence into a typed arm is trusted decoding at the driver/provider boundary, which is exactly what runtime denotes; the Core stores the arm but does not decode the native wait status. Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because the arm is committed there and is thereafter immutable. Q4: same traversal as the Process being decoded. Observed-conformance because the justification is provable only from the observed termination.
entries.traversal: one Exec dispatch and its outcome
entries.remediation: Decode the exact native termination evidence into its matching arm, and report the Process as unproven when the evidence does not justify any arm.

entries.title: Lost runtime carries an invented exit code
entries.statement: The runtimeLost termination arm is a bare variant that carries no exit code, signal, or other execution-outcome payload.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads only the shape of the ProcessTermination union arm being constructed; that is complete at the exec outcome station. Q2: the terminal Process record and its closed union are Core durable-record facts. Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because the arm is committed there. Q4: same traversal. Unrepresentable rather than reject-at-boundary: the arm is declared with no payload field, so no supported API can attach an exit code to it; the separate rule that the arm must be justified by lost-runtime evidence is the runtime-owned decoding entry.
entries.traversal: one Exec dispatch and its outcome
entries.remediation: Record runtimeLost as the bare arm and carry any native detail in the protected evidence record instead.

entries.title: Teardown leaves a Process nonterminal
entries.statement: A Stop or Delete traversal terminalizes every remaining nonterminal Process of the captured epoch with an exact recorded reason before the Sandbox is published stopped.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the captured Process set, each Process's reaped outcome, and the containment-absence proof; those facts exist only at the teardown evidence station. Q2: terminalizing the durable Process records is a Core durable-record act, distinct from the driver's containment-absence proof, which is a separate runtime-owned entry at the same station. Q3: the teardown station is the last correct point to withhold the stopped publication, and there is no later station on this traversal. Q4: same traversal as the Stop or Delete operation being described. Observed-conformance because the reaped outcomes are provable only after teardown observation.
entries.traversal: one Stop or Delete teardown traversal
entries.remediation: Reap Process outcomes, terminalize every remaining nonterminal Process with its exact reason, and only then publish the Sandbox as stopped.

entries.title: Process unknown resolved with a different execution identity or epoch
entries.statement: An unproven Process resolves to running or terminated only by reconciling the same Core launch token and, once learned, the same backend execution identity in the same runtime epoch.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the Process's durable launch token and bound runtime reference against the identity carried by the incoming evidence; the launch token, request, Process ID, and effect intent are durable before dispatch, so the fact set is complete at the exec outcome station. Q2: the launch token and Process binding are Core durable records. Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because accepting mismatched evidence commits a false resolution. Q4: same traversal. Reject-at-boundary: the comparison is between the incoming evidence's identity and a Core record.
entries.traversal: one Exec dispatch and its outcome
entries.remediation: Reject evidence bearing a different backend execution identity or runtime epoch and keep the Process unproven until matching evidence arrives.

entries.title: Authority-epoch advance or fencing used to terminalize a Process
entries.statement: Internal authority-epoch advancement or predecessor fencing removes only the ability to commit Core state; a Process becomes terminal solely on target-side fencing, a verifiable drain boundary, or other proof that it can no longer execute or produce external effects.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the advanced authority epoch, the capability's authority epoch, and the driver's fencing proof, read against the Process record at the Process outcome commit. Q2: the protected artefact is the Core Process terminal-outcome commitment, so the owner is `core`. Q3: E1 is the outcome-commit station and the last point at which an unproven terminalization can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the Process outcome commit on the Exec dispatch traversal. Merged from indices 33 and 154 (L1.D14, L2.D10, L3.D6 ref) -- one rule filed twice, on the FEN and PRC indices, for one fact set.
entries.traversal: one Exec dispatch and its outcome, at Process outcome commit
entries.remediation: Advance authority to prevent stale commits, but keep the Process unproven until target fencing or a verifiable drain boundary proves it cannot act.

entries.title: Stale running observation retained after its only observer is lost
entries.statement: A Process whose only fresh observer is lost stops being reported as running and is restored to running only from fresh same-epoch evidence.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the Process's last observation, the freshness and liveness of the observing channel, and the bound epoch; all are Core-held facts at the exec outcome station. Q2: the Process status record and its evidence freshness are Core durable records. Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct point to demote the reported state, because a stale running report authorizes callers to act on a Process that may already be gone. Q4: the runtime-side obligation to reconnect the control channel under current authority is a separate Sandbox-state entry. Reject-at-boundary: observer liveness is a Core-held fact, not external state being probed.
entries.traversal: one Exec dispatch and its outcome
entries.remediation: Demote the Process to its reconcilable state when its only fresh observer is lost, and restore running only from fresh same-epoch evidence.

entries.title: Old-epoch Process left nonterminal after runtime replacement
entries.statement: A launch traversal that replaces a runtime terminalizes every nonterminal Process of the replaced epoch with runtimeReplaced, runtimeLost, or fenced before the new epoch is published running.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the replaced epoch's Process set together with the fencing or absence evidence produced by the replacement; that evidence exists only at the launch result station. Q2: terminalizing durable Process records is a Core durable-record act.
