Q3: the launch result station is the last correct point to withhold the running publication, because publishing the new epoch while old Processes remain nonterminal leaves two live lineages. Q4: the teardown counterpart is a separate per-station entry on the Stop or Delete traversal, since a combined entry would bind launch components to a teardown pair they do not traverse. Observed-conformance because the fencing evidence is post-launch.
entries.traversal: one launch traversal that replaces an existing runtime epoch
entries.remediation: Terminalize every nonterminal Process of the replaced epoch with its exact reason before publishing the new epoch as running.

entries.title: Suspend terminalizes an accepted but undispatched Process
entries.statement: A continuity-preserving Suspend withholds launch authority from an accepted but externally undispatched Process and leaves it accepted rather than terminalizing it.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the Process's accepted state, whether its launch has been externally dispatched, and the operation's continuity-preserving kind; all three are Core durable records available at the live operation's effect station. Q2: launch authority and Process records are Core-owned. Q3: the live effect station is the last correct refusal point, because terminalization is immutable. Q4: the absence-producing counterpart, where Stop revokes authority and terminalizes the undispatched Process, is part of the teardown traversal's obligations. Reject-at-boundary under Ruling R2: no external state is consulted.
entries.traversal: one SuspendSandbox operation against an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Withhold the launch-authority grant and leave the undispatched Process accepted, so a successful same-epoch Resume can regrant it.

entries.title: Process state transition outside the locked graph
entries.statement: Process state advances only along the locked edges from accepted to starting or terminated, from starting to running, `unknown`, or terminated, from running to `unknown` or terminated, and from `unknown` to running or terminated.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the current Process state and the proposed successor state; both are complete wherever the Process record is written, and the exec outcome station is the earliest station on this traversal at which a state advance is committed. Q2: the Process state graph is a Core durable-record vocabulary. Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because the write commits there. Q4: same traversal. Unrepresentable because a generated state machine exposes only the locked edges as constructible transitions.
entries.traversal: one Exec dispatch and its outcome
entries.remediation: Advance the Process only along a locked edge, and reconcile rather than reviving a terminated Process.

entries.title: Terminated Process carries an open or absent outcome
entries.statement: Every terminated Process carries exactly one arm of the closed ProcessTermination union with that arm's declared payload, and never an absent, open, or provider-defined outcome.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the terminated Process record's outcome field against the closed union; that is complete at the exec outcome station. Q2: the terminal Process record and its closed union are Core durable-record facts. Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because the outcome is immutable once committed. Q4: same traversal; the runtime-owned rule about which arm the evidence justifies is filed separately because its fact set is native evidence rather than record shape. Unrepresentable because the generated terminated variant requires exactly one arm of the sealed union and has no open reason field.
entries.traversal: one Exec dispatch and its outcome
entries.remediation: Commit exactly one closed ProcessTermination arm and keep native codes in the protected evidence record.

entries.title: Replacement, fencing, or Stop causality asserted without target-side proof
entries.statement: The runtimeReplaced, fenced, and stoppedBySandbox termination arms are recorded only after target-side execution fencing or containment absence proves the Process cannot act, and stoppedBySandbox additionally requires proven deliberate Stop causality.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the target-side fencing or containment-absence proof and the Stop causality record against the arm being written; that proof exists only at the teardown evidence station. Q2: recording the arm on the durable Process record is a Core act; the driver's production of the absence proof is a separate runtime-owned entry at the same station. Q3: the teardown station is the last correct refusal point, and there is no later station on this traversal. Q4: same traversal as the Stop or Delete operation whose causality is being claimed. Observed-conformance because the fencing and causality facts are provable only from post-effect evidence.
entries.traversal: one Stop or Delete teardown traversal
entries.remediation: Prove target-side fencing or containment absence and deliberate Stop causality before selecting these arms, otherwise leave the Process unproven.

entries.title: Arbitrary or unadvertised signal accepted
entries.statement: A SignalProcess request selects exactly one signal from the effective capability's closed advertised set for the targeted Process, Sandbox, and runtime epoch.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the requested signal against the resolved effective capability's closed advertised signal set and the target coordinate; all are complete at the live request surface. Q2: admission of one Process-targeted operation against an existing Sandbox is the live request surface. Q3: the live request surface is the last correct refusal point, because acceptance durably commits a signal intent. Q4: the driver-side rule that the dispatch must be the exact target-specific signal action, and not an emulation by VM power controls or Sandbox deletion, is a different owner at the dispatch station and is filed separately. Reject-at-boundary: the advertised set is an immutable capability fact returned with the Sandbox.
entries.traversal: one SignalProcess request against an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Select a signal from the advertised set, or use TerminateProcess or StopSandbox when the required signal is unsupported.

entries.title: Generic signal accepted while the Sandbox is suspended
entries.statement: A generic SignalProcess request against a suspended Sandbox is admitted only when the target advertises deterministic delivery semantics under suspension, while StopSandbox remains legal.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the current Sandbox runtime state and the target's advertised suspended-delivery capability; both are Core-held facts complete at the live request surface. Q2: admission of one operation against an existing Sandbox is the live request surface. Q3: the live surface is the last correct refusal point, because acceptance commits a signal intent whose delivery semantics under quiescence are undefined. Q4: same traversal as the signal request. Reject-at-boundary under Ruling R2: current runtime state is a Core durable record, not external state being probed.
entries.traversal: one SignalProcess request against an existing suspended Sandbox
entries.remediation: Resume the Sandbox before signalling, or use StopSandbox when the target does not advertise deterministic delivery under suspension.

entries.title: Driver reports signal dispatch without invoking the exact target-specific action
entries.statement: A driver reports a signal dispatch as accepted only after invoking the exact target-specific signal action and obtaining backend acceptance evidence, never by emulating it with VM power controls, Sandbox deletion, or a coarser containment verb.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the driver's dispatch evidence — that the exact target-specific action was invoked and accepted — which exists only after the dispatch attempt. Q2: producing and decoding that native dispatch evidence is the driver/provider boundary, so runtime owns it; this also excludes emulating a missing signal with VM power controls or Sandbox deletion. Q3: the live operation's outcome station is the last correct point to withhold success. Q4: the separate rule that a successful dispatch is not delivery, handling, or exit reads the result contract alone under a different owner and is filed separately. Observed-conformance because the dispatch evidence is provable only after the effect.
entries.traversal: one SignalProcess operation against an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Prove the exact target-specific dispatch was invoked and accepted before committing success, otherwise leave the Operation nonterminal or terminalize it as `unknown`.

entries.title: Signal dispatch represented as delivery, handling, or exit
entries.statement: A successful SignalProcess Operation asserts only that the exact target-specific dispatch was invoked and accepted, and never that the signal was delivered, handled, obeyed, or that the Process exited.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the Signal Operation's declared success postcondition against the outcome being committed; both are complete at the live operation's outcome station and no further observation is needed. Q2: the declared success postcondition and the committed terminal outcome are Core durable-record facts. Q3: the live outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because the outcome is immutable once committed. Q4: the driver's obligation to produce the dispatch evidence is a distinct fact set under a different owner and is filed separately. Disposition is reject-at-boundary, not observed-conformance: the over-claim is detectable from the result contract alone.
entries.traversal: one SignalProcess operation against an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Report the Signal Operation against its dispatch postcondition and observe the Process resource separately for delivery or exit.

entries.title: Duplicate signal or termination dispatch assumed idempotent
entries.statement: Core coordinates dispatch identities where the target declares support for them, and otherwise durably records the dispatch as possibly at-least-once, never claiming backend deduplication the target does not provide.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads Core's durable dispatch record for this Operation -- the recorded dispatch-identity support for the resolved target and the prior effect-attempt entry -- both Core durable records available at the live operation's dispatch station before the repeat. Q2: the durable dispatch record and its possibly-at-least-once annotation are the control plane's own artefacts, so under Criterion O the owner is `core`; the driver-side declaration of native dispatch-identity support is filed at `25` on the driver-entry traversal. Q3: the dispatch station is the last correct refusal point, because the duplicate native call follows immediately. Q4: the general effect-retry rule requiring native idempotency or exact adoption proof is a separate fencing entry at the driver-entry boundary; this is the Signal-specific specialization at a different station under a different fact set. Reject-at-boundary: the recorded support and the prior attempt are both Core durable records at dispatch, so no fresh external observation is needed.
entries.traversal: one SignalProcess or TerminateProcess operation against an existing Sandbox, at dispatch
entries.remediation: Coordinate dispatch identities where the target supports them, otherwise record the dispatch as possibly at-least-once rather than deduplicated.

entries.title: Process termination reported before it can no longer act
entries.statement: A TerminateProcess Operation succeeds only when the Process holds an immutable terminal outcome and is proven unable to continue acting, and generic signal dispatch never silently gains wait-for-exit semantics.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the targeted Process record's terminal outcome and its inability-to-act proof against the Terminate Operation's declared success postcondition; all are Core durable records at the live operation's outcome station. Q2: the Process record, the Operation outcome, and the declared postcondition are Core-owned. Q3: the live outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because the Operation outcome is immutable once committed. Q4: the driver's graceful-then-force staging and its containment evidence are runtime-owned obligations filed separately. Reject-at-boundary: the required Process record state is a Core durable record.
entries.traversal: one TerminateProcess operation against an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Complete the graceful and force stages, record the Process terminal outcome with its inability-to-act proof, and only then commit Terminate as succeeded.

entries.title: Output cursor advanced before durable persistence
entries.statement: A durable stdout, stderr, or merged-terminal output cursor advances only after the bytes it covers are durably persisted.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the persistence commit for a byte range against the cursor advance being written; both are Core spool facts and first exist once the Process produces output, at the exec outcome station. Q2: the durable output spool and its cursors are Core durable records. Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because a published cursor is a promise of replayability that callers immediately rely on. Q4: same traversal as the Process producing the output. Reject-at-boundary: the persistence commit is a Core record.
entries.traversal: one Exec dispatch and its output stream
entries.remediation: Persist the byte range durably, then advance the cursor that covers it.

entries.title: Cross-stream ordering promised without an explicitly merged terminal stream
entries.statement: stdout and stderr have independent monotonic cursors that preserve ordering within each stream, and no cross-stream ordering is promised unless the accepted Exec selected a terminal that explicitly merges them.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the accepted Exec's stream contract and the cursor structure being published; both are complete at the exec outcome station. Q2: the stream contract and its cursors are Core durable records. Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because publishing a single interleaved cursor is what creates the false promise. Q4: same traversal. Unrepresentable because the generated output type exposes per-stream cursors and offers a merged stream only for a Process whose accepted contract selected a merging terminal.
entries.traversal: one Exec dispatch and its output stream
entries.remediation: Read each stream from its own cursor, and request a terminal at Exec when merged ordering is required.

entries.title: Replayed output chunk without a stable sequence identity
entries.statement: Every output chunk returned after reattachment from a supplied cursor carries a stable sequence identity that lets the caller deduplicate duplicate deliveries.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the chunk being emitted and the spool's stable sequence identity for that byte range; both are Core spool facts complete at the exec outcome station. Q2: the durable output spool is a Core durable record. Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because an emitted chunk without an identity cannot be deduplicated afterwards. Q4: same traversal. Reject-at-boundary: the sequence identity is a Core record fact.
entries.traversal: one Exec dispatch and its output stream, at reattachment
entries.remediation: Attach the stable sequence identity to every emitted chunk so reattachment duplicates can be discarded by the caller.

entries.title: Accepted Process input replayed
entries.statement: Accepted Process input is never replayed: no operation over an accepted, sequenced input frame re-submits it.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the accepted, sequenced Process input frame's durable record and the operation proposed against it; both are complete at the Process-control request station where the resubmission would arrive. Q2: one Process-control request inside an existing Sandbox is the exec request surface; the accepted input-frame record is the consulted fact. Q3: the request station is the last correct refusal point, because a re-submitted input frame is already ordered for a second delivery once accepted. Q4: the separate rule bounding live stdin writer leases to one per Process has its own fact set and is filed at `198`. Unrepresentable because the generated input path offers no replay operation over an accepted, sequenced input frame.
entries.traversal: one sequenced Process-control command inside an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Recover a lost response by the retained coordinate for the accepted input frame rather than by replaying the input.

entries.title: Process termination conflated with output sealing
entries.statement: Process termination and output sealing are independent facts, and end of output is authoritative only after backend exit and output drain are both proven.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the Process terminal outcome and the output seal record; both are Core durable records first available at the exec outcome station. Q2: the Process record and the output spool are Core-owned. Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because end of output becomes authoritative the moment the seal is committed there; the Stop and Delete window in which retained output is drained and sealed is covered by `191`. Q4: the driver's obligation to produce backend-exit and drain evidence is a separate runtime-owned entry. Reject-at-boundary: both facts are Core records.
entries.traversal: one Exec dispatch and its output stream
entries.remediation: Report termination and output sealing as separate facts and declare end of output only after backend exit and drain are proven.

entries.title: End of output declared without proven backend exit and drain
entries.statement: A driver supplies proven backend exit and output-drain evidence before the Core may seal a Process output stream.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the driver's backend exit observation and its drain evidence for the Process's spool; both exist only after the execution ends. Q2: producing and decoding that native evidence is the driver/provider boundary, so runtime owns it; the Core stores the seal but does not observe the backend pipe. Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because the Core seals the stream there and a seal committed without proven drain cannot be withdrawn afterwards; the driver's obligation over the Stop and Delete drain window is filed as its own runtime-owned teardown entry alongside `191`. Q4: the Core-side independence of termination and sealing is a separate entry under a different owner. Observed-conformance because the evidence is provable only after the effect.
entries.traversal: one Exec dispatch and its output stream
entries.remediation: Observe backend exit and drain the transport fully, then supply that evidence so the Core can seal the stream.

entries.title: Output truncation, limit, or expiry hidden from the caller
entries.statement: Output retention duration, byte limit, and truncation are explicit, and a read from an expired cursor returns the typed output-expired result reporting the earliest retained cursor where partial output remains.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the spool's retention and limit contract, the requested cursor, and the earliest retained cursor; all are Core spool facts complete at the exec outcome station. Q2: the durable output spool and its retention contract are Core durable records. Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because silently returning fewer bytes destroys the caller's ability to detect the gap. Q4: same traversal. Reject-at-boundary: every consulted fact is a Core record.
entries.traversal: one Exec dispatch and its output stream
entries.remediation: Return the typed output-expired result with the earliest retained cursor and record truncation explicitly instead of silently shortening the stream.

entries.title: Process-control command without its exact coordinate
entries.statement: Every WriteProcessInput, CloseProcessInput, and ResizeProcessTerminal command carries its exact Process ID, Sandbox ID, runtime epoch, writer lease, and monotonically increasing sequence number as part of the command coordinate.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the submitted command's fields against the required coordinate; that is complete at the Process-control request station. Q2: one Process request inside an existing Sandbox is the exec request surface. Q3: the request station is the last correct refusal point, because acceptance commits a receipt keyed by that coordinate. Q4: same traversal. Unrepresentable because the generated ProcessControlCommand type makes every coordinate member required, so an ordinary retryable RPC without a lease or sequence has no construction path.
entries.traversal: one sequenced Process-control command inside an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Submit the command with its complete Process-control coordinate rather than as an ordinary retryable RPC.

entries.title: Repeated Process-control sequence enqueues a duplicate command
entries.statement: A retained prior sequence resubmitted with the same canonical command recovers the same durable receipt and never enqueues a second ordered command, regardless of later Process or lease state.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the retained receipt for that lease and sequence and the submitted canonical command digest; both are Core durable records complete at the Process-control request station. Q2: the retained receipt and the ordered command log are Core durable records. Q3: the delivery station is the last correct point at which refusing to enqueue is still correct, because after enqueue the duplicate is already ordered for delivery. Q4: same traversal. Reject-at-boundary: retained-coordinate recovery precedes current Process and lease validation and consults only Core records.
entries.traversal: one sequenced Process-control command inside an existing Sandbox, through delivery
entries.remediation: Return the retained receipt for the matching lease, sequence, and canonical command instead of enqueuing the command again.

entries.title: Repeated sequence accepted with different canonical content
entries.statement: A retained prior sequence resubmitted with a different canonical command is refused as a typed Process-control conflict carrying the original and submitted digests, and dispatches no command.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the retained receipt's canonical digest and the submitted digest; both are complete at the Process-control request station. Q2: the retained receipt is a Core durable record. Q3: the request station is the last correct refusal point, because acceptance would bind one sequence to two meanings. Q4: same traversal. Reject-at-boundary: the comparison is between the request and a Core record.
entries.traversal: one sequenced Process-control command inside an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Reuse the exact canonical command for a retained sequence, and allocate the next sequence for genuinely new content.

entries.title: Out-of-order Process-control command accepted
entries.statement: A genuinely new Process-control command is accepted only at the exact next sequence for its live writer lease, and a future sequence leaving a gap is refused with its typed out-of-range result.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the lease's last accepted sequence and the submitted sequence; both are Core durable records complete at the Process-control request station. Q2: the ordered control log is a Core durable record. Q3: the request station is the last correct refusal point, because acceptance places the command in the delivery order. Q4: retained-coordinate recovery and digest conflict are separate fact sets filed as their own entries, since only a genuinely new command reaches sequencing. Reject-at-boundary: the ordering state is Core-held.
entries.traversal: one sequenced Process-control command inside an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Submit the exact next sequence for the lease, and resubmit the missing sequence before advancing.

entries.title: Writer lease controls a different Process or runtime epoch
entries.statement: A writer lease is bound to exactly one Process and runtime epoch and is never retargeted after runtime replacement, Process termination, attachment reconnection, or SDK Session rebinding.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the lease's bound Process and epoch against the command's target coordinate; both are complete at the Process-control request station. Q2: the writer-lease binding to one Process and runtime epoch is the Core durable record that grants the single-writer lane, so under Criterion O the owner is `core`. Q3: the request station is the last correct refusal point, because acceptance would order a command against the wrong execution. Q4: the adapter's obligation to make Session rebinding explicit is a different owner on the adapter traversal and is filed there. Reject-at-boundary: the lease binding is a Core record compared against the request.
entries.traversal: one sequenced Process-control command inside an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Acquire a new writer lease for the new Process and epoch instead of reusing a stale lease.

entries.title: Input receipt represented as application consumption
entries.statement: A Process-control receipt proves only that Core durably deduplicated and ordered the command and owns its delivery obligation, and never that the process consumed input bytes, that an application reacted to a terminal resize, or that the Process remains alive.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the receipt's declared meaning against the outcome being reported; both are complete at the exec outcome station where the receipt state is published. Q2: the receipt and its declared semantics are Core durable records. Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because the published receipt state is what callers act on. Q4: same traversal. Reject-at-boundary: the over-claim is detectable from the receipt contract alone with no further observation.
entries.traversal: one sequenced Process-control command inside an existing Sandbox, at receipt publication
entries.remediation: Report the receipt against its ordering and delivery meaning and observe the Process resource separately for application behaviour.

entries.title: Terminal resize accepted for a Process without a terminal or after termination
entries.statement: ResizeProcessTerminal is accepted only for a nonterminal Process whose accepted Exec selected a terminal, and travels the same ordered Process-control stream as input and close.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the accepted Exec's terminal selection and the Process's current state against the resize request; all are Core-held facts complete at the Process-control request station. Q2: the Process request surface inside an existing Sandbox is exec. Q3: the request station is the last correct refusal point, because acceptance places a resize into the control order for an execution that cannot honour it. Q4: same traversal. Reject-at-boundary under Ruling R2: the terminal selection and Process state are Core durable records, not external state.
entries.traversal: one sequenced Process-control command inside an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Request a terminal at Exec and issue resize only while the Process is nonterminal, through the ordered Process-control stream.

entries.title: Input accepted after CloseProcessInput
entries.statement: CloseProcessInput commits an irreversible ordered close record, after which any later input write for that Process is refused.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the ordered control log for a committed close record and the submitted write; both are Core durable records complete at the Process-control request station. Q2: the ordered control log is a Core durable record. Q3: the request station is the last correct refusal point, because acceptance would order a write after an irreversible close. Q4: same traversal. Reject-at-boundary: the close record is a Core record consulted before acceptance.
entries.traversal: one sequenced Process-control command inside an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Treat the close as final for that Process and start a new Exec when further input is required.

entries.title: Accepted Process-control command silently lost
entries.statement: Every accepted Process-control command terminalizes as delivered, discarded with a never-delivered proof under an exact Process-terminal rule, failed with a never-delivered proof and quiesced delivery authority, or `unknown` naming its missing proofs, and remains observable through the Process control status or retained evidence.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the accepted receipt, the delivery evidence, and the Process-terminal rule that may discard it; all are Core durable records first complete at the exec outcome station. Q2: the receipt and its outcome carrier are Core durable records. Q3: the exec outcome station is the last correct refusal point, because the command's terminal outcome is committed there and a silently dropped receipt cannot be recovered afterwards; the Stop and Delete window in which remaining Processes are terminalized and pending commands resolved is covered by `191`. Q4: same traversal as the command. Reject-at-boundary: the four outcome arms are disjoint and selectable from Core records plus the driver evidence already retained.
entries.traversal: one sequenced Process-control command inside an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Terminalize every accepted command with one of the four disjoint outcomes and keep the receipt observable rather than discarding it silently.

entries.title: Snapshot class or source disposition is omitted or provider-selected
entries.statement: Every snapshot capture request carries one exact resolved Snapshot class identity together with its complete resolved class definition and one explicit source-after-capture disposition of runtimeStatePreserved or stopped.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the canonical capture request and the content-addressed Snapshot class definition resolved for the target member; both are complete at the live request station and no driver, provider, or launch fact is consulted, so firstSoundPhase is L0. Q2: the request surface for one operation against an existing Sandbox owns the canonical request, so the owner is live, not artifact (which owns only the declared Snapshot requirement) and not core (which only stores the committed class). Q3: L0 is the last station at which refusing is a correct implementation, because a capture that reaches L1 has already committed a class identity into an immutable Snapshot manifest. Q4: the omission is committed by the capture operation whose traversal this describes, so it stays here. The disposition is unrepresentable rather than reject-at-boundary because no supported request type encodes an absent class, an absent disposition, or a provider-decides value; a named authoring profile or SDK convenience may select the class but its exact identity and complete definition still appear in the canonical request.
entries.traversal: CreateSnapshot live request against an existing Sandbox runtime
entries.remediation: Name one exact resolved Snapshot class and one explicit source-after-capture disposition in the canonical request.

entries.title: Filesystem Snapshot class relied on for runtime continuity
entries.statement: A capture or restore request derives no memory, Process, open-descriptor, clock, network-connection, or device continuity from a Snapshot class whose kind is filesystem.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the resolved class kind and component set and the continuity the request depends on; both are fully present in the canonical request at the live station, so firstSoundPhase is L0. Q2: the pairing of a resolved class against a requested continuity is a request-surface decision, so the owner is live. Q3: L0 is the last correct refusal station, because after acceptance the capture has already bound a filesystem class to a request that assumed runtime continuity and the caller can no longer be told the request was wrong rather than the outcome. Q4: the over-claim is made by the capture or restore request itself, not by a later operation. Reject-at-boundary rather than unrepresentable because a well-formed request can legally name a filesystem class and separately request continuity-dependent behaviour; the contradiction is semantic, not structural.
entries.traversal: CreateSnapshot or RestoreSandbox live request against an existing Sandbox runtime
entries.remediation: Select a runtime Snapshot class when memory, Process, descriptor, clock, connection, or device continuity is required.

entries.title: Runtime Snapshot succeeds with incomplete required components
entries.statement: A capture using a runtime Snapshot class terminalizes as succeeded only when every component its class marks required is durable and its compatibility metadata is committed.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the class-declared required component set plus the post-effect durability and compatibility evidence for each captured component; that evidence exists only after the capture effect, at the live operation's terminalization station, so firstSoundPhase is L1. Q2: publishing a terminal outcome for an accepted Operation is a Core durable-record act, so the owner is core; the driver's obligation to produce the component evidence is a separate runtime entry. Q3: L1 is where the outcome is committed and therefore the last station at which withholding succeeded is still correct on this traversal. Q4: the over-claim is committed by the capture operation itself. Observed-conformance because the completeness of the retained component set is provable only after the capture effect has run, unlike the admission checks filed at L0.
entries.traversal: CreateSnapshot live request against an existing Sandbox runtime
entries.remediation: Withhold success and report the exact missing component or uncommitted compatibility metadata until every class-required component is durable.

entries.title: Capture accepted while a Core Process is nonterminal
entries.statement: Every v1 snapshot capture and every Fork is admitted only while every Core Process bound to the source runtime epoch is terminal, because v1 Snapshot classes support only coreProcessHandling = rejectNonterminal.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the resolved class's coreProcessHandling value and the Core Process records bound to the source Sandbox ID and epoch; both are complete at the live request station, so firstSoundPhase is L0. Q2: the pairing of the request against current Core Process state is a request-surface admission decision, so the owner is live. Q3: L0 is the last station at which refusing is correct, because acceptance durably commits an operation whose class cannot describe a nonterminal Process. Q4: CreateSnapshot and ForkSandbox are both capture-class live requests reading the same fact set under the same owner at the same station, so the four-question partition yields one entry rather than two; the restored-execution successor-Process contract is a different fact set and is filed separately. Reject-at-boundary rather than dynamic-preflight under the reserved reading of that disposition: Process terminality is a Core durable record, not current external state the product does not own.
entries.traversal: CreateSnapshot or ForkSandbox live request against the source Sandbox runtime
entries.remediation: Terminate or await every Core Process in the source epoch before requesting capture or Fork.

entries.title: Preserved source changes runtime state or epoch across capture
entries.statement: A capture declaring sourceAfterCapture = runtimeStatePreserved, including every Fork, terminalizes as succeeded only when the source Sandbox finishes in its original runtime state under its original runtime epoch, with any temporary quiescence and authority fully restored and attachment or external-connection disruption recorded separately.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the source Sandbox's runtime state and epoch before and after the capture effect together with the declared disposition; the post-effect half exists only at the capture operation's own terminalization station, so firstSoundPhase is L1. Q2: the source runtime state and the retain-versus-allocate epoch decision are Core durable records, so the owner is core; the competing runtime placement confuses this rule with the driver's obligation to produce continuity evidence, and the competing R1 placement would file the source's disposition on the child's launch traversal, which this operation does not enter. Q3: L1 is where the capture outcome and the resulting source epoch are committed and therefore the last correct refusal station. Q4: the source disposition is changed by the capture or Fork operation itself, so it belongs on this traversal.
entries.traversal: CreateSnapshot or ForkSandbox live request against the source Sandbox runtime
entries.remediation: Restore the original source runtime state, epoch, and authority after quiescence, or declare a target that cannot claim the preserved postcondition.

entries.title: Snapshot omits or overrides its pinned Artifact identity
entries.statement: Every Snapshot manifest commits the exact source Artifact Set member, runtime-profile identity, and relevant immutable manifest digests resolved for the source runtime, and the capture request never supplies, substitutes, or overrides them.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the canonical capture request and the immutable Artifact and profile identities already resolved for the source Sandbox runtime; both are complete at the live station, so firstSoundPhase is L0. Q2: refusing a request that carries its own Artifact identity is a request-surface decision, so the owner is live. Q3: L0 is the last correct refusal station, because acceptance seals those identities into an immutable Snapshot manifest that later restores must match. Q4: the substitution is attempted by the capture request itself; the separate case of a restore or restore-as-create widening immutable Artifact policy is a different traversal and is filed under policy non-widening at its own station.
entries.traversal: CreateSnapshot live request against an existing Sandbox runtime
entries.remediation: Let the capture inherit the source runtime's pinned Artifact member, profile identity, and digests; construct a new Sandbox to use a different Artifact.

entries.title: Restore launch reactivates the source runtime epoch
entries.statement: A launch against an existing Sandbox -- StartSandbox, same-Sandbox Restore, or restore-as-create -- acts only under the newly allocated runtime epoch and never grants, restores, or re-enables mutation authority to any epoch that preceded it.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the durably allocated new epoch, the Sandbox's monotonic epoch high-water mark, and the authority grant the launch is about to make; all three are complete at the effect-authority station of the launch traversal, so firstSoundPhase is R0. Q2: epoch records and authority fencing are Core durable records, so the owner is core, correcting the competing runtime proposal, which describes the driver's evidence rather than the authority grant. Q3: R1 is the last station on this same traversal at which refusing to publish the restored runtime is still correct, and R0 to R1 is a direct edge. Q4: the live Restore request that authorized this launch is a different traversal carrying its own stopped-proof and epoch-allocation entries; this entry describes only the launch that request authorizes, which is why it is filed as R0 to R1 and never as C0 to R1. Reject-at-boundary rather than observed-conformance because the decision reads two Core records and requires no post-launch probe.
entries.traversal: Launch traversal authorized by StartSandbox, RestoreSandbox, or restore-as-create against an existing Sandbox.
entries.remediation: Run the restored runtime only under the newly allocated epoch and keep every prior epoch permanently fenced.

entries.title: Fork child shares source identity, authority, or an unsealed source
entries.statement: Every accepted Fork durably commits, before any capture or child-creation effect, a sealed target naming the exact immutable source Sandbox ID and source runtime epoch together with a newly preallocated child Sandbox ID; the child is a distinct Sandbox whose epoch line begins at 1 under its own mutation authority, sharing no Sandbox identity, Core Process identity, or authority coordinate with its source, and its complete Snapshot-equivalent provenance and ancestry are recorded in that same commit.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the sealed Fork target, the preallocated child Sandbox ID, the child and source Sandbox records, the Core Process records of both, and the ancestry record -- all Core durable records spanning admission through the acceptance commit. Q2: identity allocation, authority separation, and provenance records are Core durable records, so the owner is `core`. Q3: the three drafts carried L0->L0, L0->L1, and L1->L1; resolved to L0->L1, admission through the acceptance commit that publishes the preallocated child. Q4: the sharing is committed by the Fork operation itself. Merged from indices 14, 15, and 190 (L0.D1, L1.D5, L2.D9, L3.D9) -- one rule filed three times under one owner at three phase pairs, the packet's worst single defect. familyPrefix moved from IDE to FRK under the check-3 rebalance. The provenance/ancestry clause is not split out: its fact set (the sealed source coordinates) is identical to the identity-separation clause's, so Criterion P forbids a second entry.
entries.traversal: ForkSandbox acceptance traversal, from admission through the acceptance commit
entries.remediation: Seal the source Sandbox ID and epoch and preallocate a distinct child Sandbox ID at epoch 1 in the Fork acceptance commit, with independent mutation authority and full recorded provenance.

entries.title: Migration retains an epoch without an atomic fenced handoff
entries.statement: A migration retains the source runtime epoch only when Core holds proof of every locked handoff requirement and commits a definite terminal outcome for the migration Operation; every other relocation allocates a new epoch.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the six handoff proofs plus the resulting epoch decision, and the handoff proofs exist only after the transfer effect at the migration operation's own terminalization station, so firstSoundPhase is L1. Q2: retaining versus allocating an epoch is a Core durable-record and authority-fencing decision, so the owner is core. Q3: L1 is where the epoch decision and the migration outcome are committed and therefore the last correct refusal station. Q4: migration is system- or operator-originated, and under the binding ruling a system-originated Operation is filed at exactly the phase its caller-originated twin would occupy, so origin does not move it; the public-surface question of whether Migration may be admitted at all is a different fact set filed under the admission family. Observed-conformance because uninterrupted Process authority and source fencing are provable only from post-effect evidence.
entries.traversal: System- or operator-originated migration Operation against the source Sandbox runtime; system- or operator-originated; no public migration verb exists -- handoff recorded to the public-surface entry.
entries.remediation: Prove the full fenced-handoff set before retaining the epoch, or represent the transfer as a cold relocation that allocates a new epoch.

entries.title: Framework Session used as a Core identity or authority coordinate
entries.statement: Adapter Session identity stays outside the Core resource model and never appears in a Core request as a target, authority, precondition, or idempotency coordinate.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the adapter's own Session model and the closed Core coordinate vocabulary of Sandbox ID, runtime epoch, Operation ID, Process ID, Snapshot ID, etag, and idempotency key; both are complete at the adapter boundary before any Core call is formed, so firstSoundPhase is F0. Q2: Session identity is explicitly adapter-owned, so the owner is framework. Q3: F0 is the last correct refusal station, because a Session-shaped coordinate that leaves the adapter has already displaced a Core coordinate and the Core cannot recover the caller's intended target from it. Q4: the substitution happens inside the adapter, on its own ingress traversal. Unrepresentable because no Core request type has a Session-typed field, so a conforming client cannot construct the value.
entries.traversal: Framework or CLI adapter action ingress
entries.remediation: Carry SandboxRuntimeRef, Process ID, Operation ID, etag, and idempotency key explicitly and keep Session identity adapter-local.

entries.title: Framework Session resume silently retargets an old runtime or Process handle
entries.statement: A framework adapter rebinds a Session to a different runtime only explicitly, after determining which of same-epoch attachment, proven same-epoch suspended Process continuity, or replacement from retained state holds, and maps those three results respectively to reattachment, ResumeSandbox, and CreateSandbox or RestoreSandbox against a new epoch.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the adapter's stored Session binding of Sandbox ID, runtime epoch, and Process handles together with which of the three continuity proofs the provider can supply; both are complete at the adapter boundary before the Core call is formed, so firstSoundPhase is F0. Q2: reconnect-versus-rebind behaviour is explicitly adapter-owned, so the owner is framework; the Core's own never-silently-retarget rule is a separate identity-family entry at its own station. Q3: L0 is the last station on this same traversal at which refusing is still correct, because a request that pins the superseded epoch must be refused as a stale runtime by the live boundary; F0 to L0 is a direct edge. Q4: the silent rebinding is performed by the adapter, so it stays on the adapter's traversal and is linked to the Core rule by handoff rather than duplicated onto it.
entries.traversal: Framework adapter Session resume mapped onto a Core live request
entries.remediation: Determine attachment, same-epoch continuity, or replacement first, issue the exact matching Core operation, and rebind the Session explicitly.

entries.title: Adapter phase presented as authoritative Core state
entries.statement: A framework adapter presents Sandbox and Process lifecycle state only as the Core's own closed status values read from Core responses, never as an adapter-derived or provider-derived phase.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the adapter's status mapping table and the closed Core status union; both are complete at the adapter boundary, so firstSoundPhase is F0. Q2: the adapter's caller-facing presentation is adapter-owned, so the owner is framework; the parallel rule that provider evidence is not the required Core postcondition has a different fact set and a different owner and survives as a separate runtime entry at its own station. Q3: F0 is the last correct refusal station, because once the adapter has published a substitute phase the Core has no later opportunity to correct the caller's view. Q4: the substitution is made by the adapter on its own traversal.
entries.traversal: Framework or CLI adapter action ingress and result presentation
entries.remediation: Project the Core status union verbatim and keep any adapter-specific phase clearly labelled as adapter-local presentation.

entries.title: Adapter mints or rebinds an idempotency coordinate
entries.statement: A framework adapter recovers an accepted request only by resending the caller's exact canonical request under its original idempotency key, and never substitutes a new key, a new canonical request, or a reused key for a canonically different intent.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the adapter's key-derivation rule and the canonical request it is about to send; both are complete at the adapter boundary, so firstSoundPhase is F0. Q2: the adapter's derivation rule is adapter-owned even though the resulting binding is not, so the owner is framework; the stored key-to-digest-to-handle binding is a Core durable record and is filed as a separate core entry. Q3: F0 is the last correct refusal station, because an adapter that mints a fresh key for the same intent presents the Core with what is, by contract, a legitimately new intent, and no later boundary can distinguish the two. Q4: the derivation is performed by the adapter on its own traversal.
entries.traversal: Framework or CLI adapter action ingress
entries.remediation: Reuse the caller's original idempotency key with the byte-identical canonical request when recovering, and derive a fresh key only for a genuinely new intent.

entries.title: Adapter advertises its own mutation serialization guarantee
entries.statement: A framework adapter advertises no ordering, exclusion, or serialization guarantee for Core mutations beyond the Core's published operation-pair compatibility and precondition contract.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the adapter's declared concurrency behaviour and the Core's published compatibility and precondition contract; both are complete at the adapter boundary, so firstSoundPhase is F0. Q2: what an adapter advertises to its own callers is adapter-owned, so the owner is framework; the Core's lane-authority rule for two incompatible concurrent mutations is a separate core entry at its own station. Q3: F0 is the last correct refusal station, because the guarantee is consumed by the caller before any Core call is made and the Core has no way to retract it. Q4: the over-claim is made by the adapter on its own traversal.
entries.traversal: Framework or CLI adapter tool registration and action ingress
entries.remediation: Document exactly the Core's compatibility and precondition contract and use etag and runtime-epoch preconditions instead of an adapter-local lock.

entries.title: Adapter adds a public error variant
entries.statement: An adapter's caller-visible failure type is exactly the Core's closed public error, known-failure, and ambiguity union projected into the host language, with no added, merged, renamed, or provider-defined semantic variant.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the adapter's declared public failure type and the Core's closed public union; both are complete at the adapter boundary, so firstSoundPhase is F0. Q2: the adapter's language-specific typed errors are adapter-owned, so the owner is framework; the Core rule forbidding open or provider-defined public reasons is a separate error-surface entry at its own station. Q3: F0 is the last correct refusal station, because the variant is part of the adapter's published type and is observed by callers before any Core call. Q4: the addition is made by the adapter on its own traversal. Unrepresentable because the adapter's failure type is generated from the closed Core union, so a conforming adapter cannot construct an extra variant; a hand-written variant is a generation-boundary violation rather than a runtime value.
entries.traversal: Framework or CLI adapter error projection
entries.remediation: Generate the adapter failure type from the closed Core union and express adapter-specific context as non-semantic annotation.

entries.title: Adapter reinterprets a transport timeout as a Core outcome
entries.statement: An adapter surfaces a transport timeout, transport cancellation, or connection loss as the transport condition it is, never as a Core Operation failure, a proven Core cancellation, or a Process outcome.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the transport condition the adapter observed and the Core result contract's distinction between transport conditions, accepted outcomes, and ambiguity arms; both are complete at the adapter boundary, so firstSoundPhase is F0. Q2: converting transport conditions into caller-visible results is adapter-owned, so the owner is framework; the Core-side forbidden inference that an RPC deadline is an Operation failure or a Process deadline outcome is carried by the core outcome-legality entries at their own stations. Q3: F0 is the last correct refusal station, because the conversion is complete inside the adapter and the Core never sees it. Q4: the inference is drawn by the adapter on its own traversal.
entries.traversal: Framework or CLI adapter error projection
entries.remediation: Report the transport condition distinctly and resolve the Operation or Process state by retrieving it from the Core.

entries.title: Adapter collapses Process exit into infrastructure failure
entries.statement: An adapter reports a Core Process termination arm exactly as the Core published it and never collapses a nonzero exit, signal termination, or deadline outcome into an adapter or infrastructure error.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Core-published ProcessTermination arm and the adapter's caller-visible mapping of it; both are complete at the adapter boundary once the Core result is in hand, so firstSoundPhase is F0. Q2: the mapping into host-language results is adapter-owned, so the owner is framework; the driver's obligation to justify the arm from exact native evidence is a separate runtime entry at its own station. Q3: F0 is the last correct refusal station, because the collapse is entirely internal to the adapter. Q4: the collapse is performed by the adapter on its own traversal.
entries.traversal: Framework or CLI adapter Process result projection
entries.remediation: Surface the exact ProcessTermination arm and exit code as a normal Process result, reserving infrastructure errors for infrastructure conditions.

entries.title: Adapter auto-replays an ambiguous effect
entries.statement: An adapter never converts a Core ambiguity outcome into a replacement effect, and resolves ambiguity only by surfacing the ambiguity arm to the caller, by Core observation, or by Core idempotent recovery of the same coordinate.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Core-published ambiguity arm for the prior effect attempt and the adapter's retry policy; both are complete at the adapter boundary, so firstSoundPhase is F0. Q2: the retry policy is adapter-owned, so the owner is framework; the Core rule that an accepted Process is never automatically replaced after ambiguity is a separate core entry at its own station. Q3: F0 is the last correct refusal station, because a replay carrying a fresh idempotency coordinate is by contract a legitimately new intent that no downstream boundary can or should refuse. Q4: the replay is initiated by the adapter, so it is filed on the adapter's traversal and linked to the core rule by handoff.
entries.traversal: Framework or CLI adapter recovery path after an ambiguous Core outcome
entries.remediation: Surface the ambiguity arm, or recover the same coordinate through Core idempotency or Core observation, instead of issuing a replacement effect.

entries.title: Adapter asserts provider fencing or cleanup proof
entries.statement: An adapter reports fencing, containment absence, and cleanup completion only as the proof the Core published, and never derives, infers, or asserts such proof from provider or adapter observation.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Core-published proof obligations and outcome for the operation and the adapter's own observations; both are complete at the adapter boundary once the Core result is in hand, so firstSoundPhase is F0. Q2: provider fencing and cleanup proof are explicitly not adapter-owned, but the false assertion is the adapter's caller-facing act, so the owner is framework. Q3: F0 is the last correct refusal station, because the assertion is consumed by the caller and the Core never observes it. Q4: the assertion is made by the adapter on its own traversal; the Core and driver proof obligations are filed separately at their own stations.
entries.traversal: Framework or CLI adapter result presentation
entries.remediation: Report only the Core Operation's published proof and outcome, and mark any adapter observation explicitly as non-authoritative.

entries.title: Adapter composite presented as one Core Operation
entries.statement: An adapter convenience composite such as attach or Stop-then-Delete is expressed as the exact declared sequence of named Core operations, surfaces every constituent Operation handle to the caller, and never presents itself as one Core Operation or one Core outcome.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the composite's declared step sequence and the closed Core method union; both are complete at the adapter boundary, so firstSoundPhase is F0. Q2: explicit composites are named as adapter-owned, so the owner is framework; the Core rule excluding compound public verbs from the method surface is a separate admission entry at its own station. Q3: F0 is the last correct refusal station, because the composite's shape is fixed before the first Core call and each constituent call the Core sees is individually valid. Q4: the concealment is performed by the adapter on its own traversal.
entries.traversal: Framework or CLI adapter composite action ingress
entries.remediation: Issue and surface each named Core operation and its Operation handle separately, and label the composite as an adapter helper.

entries.title: Desired-state reconciler reaches the Core without etag and epoch preconditions or hides its system-originated Operations
entries.statement: A managed desired-state reconciler reaches the Core only by issuing named Core operations under etag and runtime-epoch preconditions, and exposes its system-originated Operations for observation.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the reconciler's declared action set and record model together with the Core Operation and lifecycle contract; both are complete at the Managed-Sandbox Service Definition station, so firstSoundPhase is S0. Q2: the managed layer is the Managed-Sandbox Service Definition owner, so the owner is service. Q3: L0 is the last station on this same traversal at which refusing is still correct, because a reconciler action that reaches the Core as a live request must be refused there if it carries no etag or runtime-epoch precondition; S0 to L0 is a direct edge. Q4: the unguarded Core action and the concealment are performed by the managed controller, so they are filed on the managed traversal; the reconciler's rewriting of a predecessor Operation's terminal result is filed separately at `196`, and the core filing of system-originated Operations at their caller-originated twin's phase remains a separate core entry.
entries.traversal: Managed desired-state reconciliation issuing Core operations
entries.remediation: Issue named Core operations under etag and runtime-epoch preconditions, and expose the reconciler's system-originated Operations for observation.

entries.title: Start accepted against a Sandbox without a durable stopped proof
entries.statement: `StartSandbox` is admitted only against a Sandbox holding a current durable stopped proof, and never restarts a runtime that is still present under an unretired epoch.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Start request and the Sandbox's current durable stopped proof, both complete at live admission. Q2: the invalid state is an admitted live request against an existing Sandbox, so the owner is `live` under Criterion O. Q3: L0 is the last station at which refusing still prevents a second runtime from being launched over an unretired epoch. Q4: the offending act is the StartSandbox request, so it stays on the live traversal. Filed under L0.D0: the packet avoided the forbidden C0→R1 shape by dropping StartSandbox coverage rather than filing it correctly.
entries.traversal: one StartSandbox request against an existing Sandbox
entries.remediation: Observe a current durable stopped proof before issuing StartSandbox; stop the present runtime and let its epoch retire first.

entries.title: Start authorizes a launch without fencing the prior runtime epoch
entries.statement: A Start commits its launch authorization only after the Sandbox's prior runtime epoch is permanently fenced, so no predecessor authority can commit Core state or act against the new epoch.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the prior runtime epoch's fencing record and the launch authorization about to be committed, both Core durable records at the acceptance commit. Q2: authority fencing and lane grants are the control plane's own durable artefacts, so the owner is `core` under Criterion O. Q3: L1 is the acceptance commit and the last station at which an unfenced authorization can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the Start's own acceptance commit. Filed under L0.D0.
entries.traversal: StartSandbox live-mutation traversal, at acceptance commit
entries.remediation: Permanently fence the prior runtime epoch and its authority before committing the Start's launch authorization.

entries.title: Start-authorized launch reuses a stale resolved manifest
entries.statement: The launch a Start authorizes re-resolves the Sandbox's Artifact, member, and runtime-profile manifest at the launch stage and refuses to launch from a stale or absent resolution.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Sandbox's Artifact, member, and runtime-profile references and the manifest resolution produced for this launch, both complete at manifest re-resolution. Q2: the invalid state is an expressible launch request whose resolved manifest is stale or absent, decided from the request-resolution schema, so the owner is `create` under Criterion O. Q3: C0 is the last station at which refusing still prevents a launch from a stale resolution. Q4: the offending act is the launch-request resolution itself. Filed under L0.D0.
entries.traversal: launch traversal authorized by StartSandbox, at manifest re-resolution
entries.remediation: Re-resolve the Artifact, member, and runtime-profile manifest at the launch stage and refuse to launch from a stale or absent resolution.

entries.title: Launch dispatched without operator re-admission of its resolved placement
entries.statement: A launch is dispatched only after the operator admission plane re-admits its resolved placement, capacity, and tier for the current epoch; a placement admitted for a prior launch never carries forward.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the resolved placement, capacity, and tier for the current epoch and the operator admission plane's current admission record, complete from operator re-admission. Q2: operator capability and placement admission are the operator boundary. Q3: D0 is the dispatch station and the last point at which an unadmitted placement can be refused. Q4: the offending act is this launch's own dispatch. Filed under L0.D0; `O0` was used as a firstSoundPhase by zero of the 204 draft entries.
entries.traversal: launch traversal, from operator re-admission through driver dispatch
entries.remediation: Re-admit the resolved placement, capacity, and tier at the operator admission plane for the current epoch before dispatching the launch.

entries.title: Process identifier or output cursor used as an exec identity or authority coordinate
entries.statement: Every output and event cursor on the exec branch is an observation position only, and the Core Process ID is the sole Process identity coordinate; neither is accepted in an identity, target, precondition, or authority position, and a native execution identifier is accepted in none of them.
entries.rationale: Q1: the fact is the declared domain of each exec-branch coordinate at the boundary that decodes it, complete at the exec request surface. Q2: the invalid state is an expressible exec request, so the owner is `exec` under Criterion O. Q3: E0 is the decoding station and the last point at which a wrong-domain coordinate can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the caller's exec or Process-control request. Split out of M8 because output cursors live at `process.status.output.cursor` on the exec branch and L0 and E1 are mutually unreachable (L0.D2).
entries.traversal: Exec and Process-control request traversal, at semantic decoding
entries.remediation: Carry output and event cursors only in observation requests and use the Core Process ID as the sole Process identity coordinate.

entries.title: Process observation or wait deadline mutating or terminalizing its target
entries.statement: A `WaitProcess`, `GetProcess`, or `ReadProcessOutput` deadline ends only that observation and never cancels, mutates, terminalizes, or advances the durable state of the observed Process or its output stream.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the observation deadline and the durable Process and output records it observes, both Core durable records at the exec outcome station. Q2: durable Process records and output cursors are Core-owned. Q3: E1 is the last station at which a deadline-driven mutation of the observed Process can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the Process observation itself. Split out of `67` because L0 and E1 are mutually unreachable, so a Process-resource observation can never be revalidated from L0 (L0.D2).
entries.traversal: one Process observation (WaitProcess, GetProcess, ReadProcessOutput) against an existing Process
entries.remediation: Return the observation result with the latest Process record and an explicit condition-met flag; leave the observed Process and its output stream unchanged.

entries.title: Teardown rewrites a committed Process terminal outcome
entries.statement: Sandbox teardown retains every late signal acknowledgement, reaper observation, and provider event arriving during Stop or Delete as evidence linked to the Process, and never applies it as a rewrite of a committed Process terminal outcome.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the committed Process terminal outcome and the late evidence arriving during teardown, both Core durable records on the teardown traversal. Q2: durable Process records and terminal outcomes are Core-owned. Q3: T0 is the teardown station and the last point at which a rewrite can be refused. Q4: the offending act belongs to the Stop or Delete traversal, not to the Exec traversal. This is the T0 half that `146` was borrowing the `E1→T0` edge to reach; cross-operation succession is a handoff record, never a phase edge (L0.D3).
entries.traversal: Sandbox teardown traversal during Stop or Delete, at late-evidence resolution
entries.remediation: Link late acknowledgements, reaper observations, and provider events to the Process as evidence and leave the committed terminal outcome unchanged.

entries.title: Teardown discards retained output or an accepted Process-control command
entries.statement: Sandbox teardown drains and seals retained Process output and resolves every accepted Process-control command with one of its four declared terminal outcomes; nothing accepted is silently discarded by Stop or Delete.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the retained output spool, the accepted Process-control receipts, and their outcome carriers, all Core durable records on the teardown traversal. Q2: the output spool and the control-command receipts are Core-owned. Q3: T0 is the teardown station and the last point at which a silent discard can be refused. Q4: the offending act belongs to the Stop or Delete traversal. This is the T0 half of `171`, `172`, and `182`, which were borrowing the `E1→T0` edge to reach it (L0.D3).
entries.traversal: Sandbox teardown traversal during Stop or Delete, at output seal and Process-control resolution
entries.remediation: Drain and seal retained output and resolve every accepted Process-control command with one of its four declared terminal outcomes before completing teardown.

entries.title: Live external effect attempted before its recovery classification is recorded
entries.statement: Before dispatching any external effect on the live-mutation traversal, Core durably records the attempt with its exact parameters together with one of the four locked recovery classes — no durable intent, provider idempotency token available, external identity discoverable for adoption, or none available — and reports ambiguity with quarantine when no class applies.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the effect parameters and the driver's declared effect class, together with the Core-held attempt record; all are available from live admission through the effect commit. Q2: the durable effect-attempt record and its classification are Core durable records. Q3: L1 is the last station at which refusing still prevents an unclassified live dispatch. Q4: the offending act is the live mutation's own dispatch. Added because `60` narrows to the launch branch, and D0→R0 reaches neither L1 nor E1 (L0.D8); this mirrors the three-way split already used for acceptance commits (`37` C0→D0, `38` L0→L1, `39` E0→E1).
entries.traversal: live Sandbox mutation traversal, at external effect-attempt recording preceding dispatch
entries.remediation: Durably record the attempt and one of the four locked recovery classes before dispatching the live external effect, and quarantine the attempt as ambiguous when no class applies.

entries.title: Exec external effect attempted before its recovery classification is recorded
entries.statement: Before dispatching any external effect on the Exec traversal, Core durably records the attempt with its exact parameters together with one of the four locked recovery classes — no durable intent, provider idempotency token available, external identity discoverable for adoption, or none available — and reports ambiguity with quarantine when no class applies.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the effect parameters and the driver's declared effect class, together with the Core-held attempt record; all are available from Exec admission through the dispatch commit. Q2: the durable effect-attempt record and its classification are Core durable records. Q3: E1 is the last station at which refusing still prevents an unclassified exec dispatch. Q4: the offending act is the Exec's own dispatch. Added because `60` narrows to the launch branch, and D0→R0 reaches neither L1 nor E1 (L0.D8); this mirrors the three-way split already used for acceptance commits (`37` C0→D0, `38` L0→L1, `39` E0→E1).
entries.traversal: Exec traversal, at external effect-attempt recording preceding dispatch
entries.remediation: Durably record the attempt and one of the four locked recovery classes before dispatching the exec external effect, and quarantine the attempt as ambiguous when no class applies.

entries.title: Signal Operation committed `succeeded` without its three-part proof
entries.statement: A `SignalProcess` Operation commits `succeeded` only when the Sandbox ID, Process ID, runtime epoch, and authority were validated, the exact target was selected, and returned driver evidence proves the target-specific dispatch was accepted; any weaker knowledge set leaves the Operation nonterminal or terminalizes it `unknown`.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the validated coordinates, the selected target, and the driver evidence returned after dispatch; the last exists only after the effect. Q2: terminal-outcome commitment is the control plane's own durable artefact, so the owner is `core`. Q3: L1 is the Operation outcome commit and the last point at which an unproven `succeeded` can be withheld. Q4: the driver's obligation to invoke the exact target-specific action is the other half of the seam, filed at the edited `163` (`runtime`). This completes the two-owner seam L1.D8 declared, mirroring the Suspend precedent (`103` core / `104` runtime).
entries.traversal: one SignalProcess operation against an existing Sandbox, at Operation outcome commit
entries.remediation: Commit `succeeded` only on validated coordinates, exact target selection, and returned driver acceptance evidence; otherwise leave the Operation nonterminal or terminalize it `unknown`.

entries.title: Managed desired-state revision or restart policy carried in a Core request field
entries.statement: A managed layer's desired-state revision and its restart/recreate policy live in the managed layer's own records; no Core request type carries either, so the Core never becomes a perpetual desired-state orchestrator.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the declared shape of the Core request types and the managed layer's own desired-state records, both complete at the service station. Q2: the Managed-Sandbox Service boundary owns its desired-state records, so the owner is `service`. Q3: S0 is the service station and the only point at which the unrepresentable input can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the managed layer's own request shape. Split out as clause (a) of `203` (L1.D17); `S0→S0` is introduced by this entry.
entries.traversal: Managed-Sandbox Service request-shape traversal
entries.remediation: Keep the desired-state revision and the restart/recreate policy in the managed layer's own records and drive the Core only through named Core operations.

entries.title: Reconciler rewrites a predecessor Operation's terminal result
entries.statement: A reconciler that must correct a completed Core action appends a new linked successor Operation and never rewrites, reopens, or reinterprets a predecessor Operation's committed terminal result.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the predecessor Operation's committed terminal result and the correction the reconciler proposes, both complete from the service station through live admission. Q2: the reconciler's own conduct against the Core surface is the Managed-Sandbox Service boundary, so the owner is `service`. Q3: L0 is the last station at which a rewrite request can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the reconciler's request. Split out as clause (c) of `203` (L1.D17).
entries.traversal: Managed desired-state reconciliation issuing Core operations against a completed predecessor Operation
entries.remediation: Append a new linked successor Operation instead of rewriting, reopening, or reinterpreting a predecessor's committed terminal result.

entries.title: Driver reports a migration handoff without its target-side proofs
entries.statement: A driver executing a migration handoff returns evidence of compatible source and destination, exclusive target-enforced authority transfer, a fenced or terminated source, uninterrupted Process authority, routing handoff, and explicit disposition of open attachments and external connections, and refuses the transfer when it cannot produce all six.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the six target-side handoff proofs, which exist only after the driver executes the handoff. Q2: producing and decoding that native evidence is the driver/provider boundary, so the owner is `runtime` under Criterion O. Q3: L1 is the last station at which the evidence can be withheld before Core retains the source epoch. Q4: the Core-side proof holding and terminal-outcome commitment are the other half of the seam, filed at the edited `191` (`core`). Completes the two-owner seam L1.D16 declared but never filed.
entries.traversal: migration handoff traversal, at driver evidence return
entries.remediation: Return all six target-side handoff proofs, or refuse the transfer and let Core represent the relocation as one that allocates a new epoch.

entries.title: More than one live stdin writer lease for one Process
entries.statement: At most one live stdin writer lease exists for a Process at any time, and a Process-control command bearing a lease that is not the current live lease is refused with the typed lease-conflict result.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Process's current live lease record and the lease the submitted command carries, both Core durable records at the Process-control admission station. Q2: the lease binding is a Core durable record. Q3: E0 is the admission station and the last point at which a conflicting lease can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the Process-control command itself. Split out of `170` (L3.D11), which keeps only the non-replay clause at `unrepresentable`. Note: lease issue, expiry, renewal, transfer, and takeover are open design work; this entry asserts exclusivity as a boundary check, not as a generated type guarantee.
entries.traversal: one sequenced Process-control command inside an existing Sandbox, at lease validation
entries.remediation: Acquire or take over the single live writer lease explicitly, and refuse commands bearing any other lease with the typed lease-conflict result.

entries.title: Create idempotency coordinate rebound to a different intent
entries.statement: One authenticated scope, method, and idempotency key binds exactly one canonical CreateSandbox request digest for its published recovery window; a replay under the same coordinate with a different canonical digest is refused as a conflict and dispatches no effect.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the stored idempotency binding and the canonical digest of the submitted request, both Core durable records at the creation acceptance station. Q2: idempotency binding and tombstone records are the control plane's own durable artefacts, so the owner is `core`. Q3: C0 is the last station at which refusing still prevents a rebound coordinate from authorizing an effect. Q4: the offending act is the Create replay itself. Closes L3.D3: the create surface never traverses L0, so the live entry `46` could not cover it, and the cross-reference to a 'creation-scope entry' pointed at nothing in the 204.
entries.traversal: CreateSandbox acceptance traversal, at idempotency binding
entries.remediation: Refuse a replay whose canonical digest differs from the one already bound to the coordinate, and use a fresh idempotency key for a different intent.

entries.title: Restore widens immutable Artifact policy
entries.statement: A same-Sandbox `RestoreSandbox` uses the exact immutable environment, filesystem, network, identity, device, secret, and target-profile policy pinned by the Sandbox's Artifact, and never replaces or widens any of them.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Restore request and the immutable policy pinned by the Sandbox's Artifact, both complete at live admission. Q2: the invalid state is an admitted live request against an existing Sandbox, so the owner is `live` under Criterion O. Q3: L0 is the last station at which a widening restore can be refused, because acceptance allocates a new runtime epoch. Q4: the offending act is the Restore request. Added under L3.D4 to discharge TAXONOMY-38 and RESULT-45 on the live restore surface.
entries.traversal: one RestoreSandbox request against an existing Sandbox, at live admission
entries.remediation: Restore under the exact policy pinned by the Sandbox's Artifact, and create a new Sandbox from a different Artifact when different policy is needed.

entries.title: Restore-as-create widens immutable Artifact policy
