entries.statement: A restore-as-create request selects or refines permitted access within the pinned Artifact's hard policy and never replaces or widens immutable environment, filesystem, network, identity, device, secret, or target-profile policy.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the restore-as-create request and the pinned Artifact's hard policy, both complete at creation acceptance. Q2: the invalid state is an expressible creation request, so the owner is `create` under Criterion O. Q3: C0 is the last station at which a widening creation can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the restore-as-create request itself. Added under L3.D4 as the creation-surface sibling of A17, because the create surface never traverses L0.
entries.traversal: restore-as-create CreateSandbox acceptance traversal, at policy resolution
entries.remediation: Select or refine only permitted access within the pinned Artifact's hard policy, and never replace or widen an immutable policy dimension at creation.

entries.title: `sourceAfterCapture = stopped` published without the full Stop postcondition
entries.statement: A capture declaring `sourceAfterCapture = stopped` publishes that disposition only after the full Stop postcondition holds for the source: every Process terminal, containment absence proven, and the prior epoch unable to act.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the source's Process terminality, the driver's containment-absence proof, and the prior epoch's fencing, which exist only after the capture acts. Q2: the published source disposition is a Core durable record. Q3: L1 is the capture commit and the last point at which an unproven `stopped` disposition can be withheld. Q4: filed on the CreateSnapshot traversal, as Q4 requires — removed from `117`, whose T0→T0 teardown pair selects components a capture never traverses (L3.D5).
entries.traversal: CreateSnapshot capture traversal, at source-disposition publication
entries.remediation: Publish `stopped` only after every Process is terminal, containment absence is proven, and the prior epoch can no longer act.

entries.title: Snapshot class identity disagrees with its resolved kind, components, or treatments
entries.statement: A Snapshot's resolved class identity agrees with its declared kind, captured component set, external-storage state, secret treatment, compatibility envelope, quiescence state, device state, portability, and Process handling; any disagreement fails capture admission.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the declared Snapshot class and the resolved kind, components, and treatments the capture request names, all complete at capture admission. Q2: the invalid state is an admitted live capture request, so the owner is `live` under Criterion O. Q3: L0 is the last station at which a disagreeing class identity can be refused, because acceptance publishes the class. Q4: the offending act is the capture request. Added under L2.D0 to discharge the previously uncited TAXONOMY-27.
entries.traversal: one CreateSnapshot request against an existing Sandbox, at capture admission
entries.remediation: Declare a class whose kind, component set, external-storage state, secret treatment, compatibility envelope, quiescence, device state, portability, and Process handling all agree, or refuse the capture.

entries.title: Snapshot deleted while an exact reference or retention hold protects it
entries.statement: `DeleteSnapshot` is admitted only when no exact reference and no retention hold protects the Snapshot, and the refusal names the protecting references.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the DeleteSnapshot request, the Snapshot's exact reference set, and its retention holds, all Core durable records complete at live admission. Q2: the invalid state is an admitted live request against an existing Snapshot, so the owner is `live` under Criterion O. Q3: L0 is the last station at which a protected deletion can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the DeleteSnapshot request. Added under L2.D0 to discharge the previously uncited TAXONOMY-35; the packet contained no DeleteSnapshot entry at all.
entries.traversal: one DeleteSnapshot request against an existing Snapshot, at live admission
entries.remediation: Release the protecting references and retention holds before issuing DeleteSnapshot; the refusal names the exact protecting references.

entries.title: Suspend or Resume accepted without the paired same-epoch continuity capability
entries.statement: `SuspendSandbox` and `ResumeSandbox` are admitted only against a runtime whose conformed target advertises the paired same-epoch suspend-and-resume continuity capability; a target advertising one without the other admits neither.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Suspend or Resume request and the conformed target's advertised continuity capability, both complete at live admission. Q2: the invalid state is an admitted live request against an existing Sandbox, so the owner is `live` under Criterion O. Q3: L0 is the last station at which an unsupported Suspend or Resume can be refused. Q4: the offending act is the caller's request. Added under L2.D0 to discharge the previously uncited TAXONOMY-24.
entries.traversal: one SuspendSandbox or ResumeSandbox request against an existing Sandbox, at live admission
entries.remediation: Admit Suspend and Resume only against a conformed target advertising both halves of the same-epoch continuity capability; otherwise use StopSandbox and StartSandbox.

entries.title: Statically absent cross-target capability deferred to launch without an explicit target branch
entries.statement: A cross-target capability, semantic, or ceiling that is statically absent from an enabled target is rejected during Artifact validation unless the Artifact declares an explicit named target branch for it, and is never deferred to workload launch or runtime discovery.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the Artifact's enabled target set and the statically declared capability, semantic, and ceiling surfaces of each target, all complete at Artifact authoring and validation. Q2: declarative static facts are the Artifact boundary. Q3: A1 is the validation station and the last point at which a statically absent capability can be refused before launch. Q4: the offending act is the Artifact authoring itself. Added under L2.D15: TAXONOMY-46 is struck from `144`, which does not state it, and is filed here with RESULT-44.
entries.traversal: Artifact authoring and validation traversal
entries.remediation: Declare an explicit named target branch in the Artifact for every statically absent cross-target capability, semantic, or ceiling instead of deferring it to launch or runtime discovery.

entries.title: Driver reports Snapshot capture success without per-component durability evidence
entries.statement: A driver reports a runtime Snapshot capture successful only after returning per-component durability and compatibility-metadata evidence for every component the resolved class marks required, and otherwise reports failure naming the exact missing component.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the per-component durability and compatibility-metadata evidence, which exist only after the capture executes. Q2: producing and decoding that native evidence is the driver/provider boundary, so the owner is `runtime` under Criterion O. Q3: L1 is the capture commit and the last point at which success can be withheld. Q4: the Core-side completeness rule is the other half of the seam, filed at `185` (`core`), whose rationale declared this counterpart and never filed it (L1.D20).
entries.traversal: CreateSnapshot capture traversal, at driver evidence return
entries.remediation: Return per-component durability and compatibility-metadata evidence for every required component, or report failure naming the exact missing component.

entries.title: Launch-branch compensating effect represented as rollback
entries.statement: A compensating effect on the launch traversal is recorded as a new forward effect with its own durable record, evidence, and outcome, never as erasure, reversal, or negation of the compensated Operation's external history.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the compensated Operation's external effect ledger and the compensating effect's own Operation record, both Core durable records at the launch-result station. Q2: the Operation record and its external effect ledger are Core-owned. Q3: R1 is the last station on the launch traversal at which a rollback representation can be refused. Q4: the offending act belongs to the launch traversal, not the teardown traversal that `66` now covers. Added under L0.D12 as the launch-branch sibling; the live and exec compensation strategies are carried by A9/A10's four locked recovery classes.
entries.traversal: launch-traversal compensating-effect recording against a prior Operation, at R1
entries.remediation: Record launch-branch compensation as a new linked forward effect with its own durable record, evidence, and outcome; never mark the compensated Operation or its external effects as reversed.

entries.title: Terminal Operation result rewritten on a live reconciliation traversal
entries.statement: An Operation's committed terminal outcome and its payload are immutable on the live mutation traversal, and later evidence, reconciliation, adoption, quarantine, or cleanup resolving at the live outcome station may only append a linked successor record that references the unchanged predecessor.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the existing terminal Operation record and the proposed write; both are Core durable records available at the live outcome station and no new observation is needed to refuse the rewrite. Q2: durable Operation records and terminal outcomes are the control plane's own artefacts, so under Criterion O the owner is `core`. Q3: L1 is the live traversal's own resolution station and the last point on that traversal at which the rewrite can be refused. Q4: the offending write belongs to the live reconciliation traversal described here; the launch-branch station is `51` and the teardown station is the T0 sibling. `reject-at-boundary`: immutability is decided from two stored records, not proved after an effect. Added because `51`'s traversal was narrowed to the launch branch and a reconciliation entering at L0 never reaches R1.
entries.traversal: Live reconciliation/adoption traversal resolving against an existing terminal Operation, at L1
entries.remediation: Append a linked successor resolution Operation instead of rewriting the predecessor's terminal outcome.

entries.title: Terminal Operation result rewritten on a teardown or cleanup reconciliation traversal
entries.statement: An Operation's committed terminal outcome and its payload are immutable on the teardown and cleanup traversal, and later evidence, reconciliation, adoption, quarantine, or cleanup resolving at teardown may only append a linked successor record that references the unchanged predecessor.
entries.rationale: Q1: the deciding facts are the existing terminal Operation record and the proposed write; both are Core durable records available at the teardown sink and no new observation is needed to refuse the rewrite. Q2: durable Operation records and terminal outcomes are the control plane's own artefacts, so under Criterion O the owner is `core`. Q3: T0 is the teardown traversal's sink and the last point at which the rewrite can be refused. Q4: the offending write belongs to the teardown or cleanup traversal described here; the launch-branch station is `51` and the live station is the L1 sibling. `reject-at-boundary`: immutability is decided from two stored records. Added because `51`'s traversal was narrowed to the launch branch and a teardown or cleanup reconciliation never reaches R1.
entries.traversal: Teardown/cleanup reconciliation traversal resolving against an existing terminal Operation, at T0
entries.remediation: Append a linked successor resolution Operation instead of rewriting the predecessor's terminal outcome.

entries.title: Verb-derived presentation label stored as Sandbox state on a launch traversal
entries.statement: On a launch traversal, Sandbox runtime state is exactly one of `provisioning`, `running`, `suspended`, `stopped`, or `unknown`; every derived launch presentation label -- creating, starting, restoring -- is recomputed at read time from the durable Operation and that authoritative status, and is never independently stored or used as the serialization oracle.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the durable Operation kind and the authoritative Core runtime status at the launch Operation and status commit station. Q2: the protected artefact is the Core durable status record and its serialization oracle, so under Criterion O the owner is `core`. Q3: R1 is the launch traversal's commit station, at which a stored launch presentation label would first become durable. Q4: the offending act is the launch traversal's own commit; the live half is `86`, whose traversal is narrowed to live lifecycle mutations, and the request-input clause of LIFECYCLE-03 stays at L0. Unrepresentable because the generated status type has no field in which a presentation label can be stored. Added because a launch traversal never reaches L1, so `86` could not bind launch-branch status commits.
entries.traversal: one launch (Create running, Start, or same-Sandbox Restore) traversal, at Operation and status commit
entries.remediation: Derive launch presentation words at read time from the Operation kind and the authoritative status, and store neither.

entries.title: Unprovable launch runtime state approximated as stopped or running
entries.statement: When a launch traversal cannot safely establish runtime presence or absence, claimed-epoch continuity, exclusive effect authority, containment emptiness, or external-effect liveness, the committed Sandbox runtime state is `unknown` with execution admission `closed`.
entries.rationale: Q1: the facts are the evidence set gathered for this launch weighed against the five presence, continuity, authority, containment, and liveness predicates, complete only at the launch result station. Q2: the published runtime state is a Core durable record, so under Criterion O the owner is `core`. Q3: R1, because the approximation becomes authoritative the moment launch publishes it and would then admit Exec against the new epoch. Q4: the same launch commits the approximation; the live half is `94`, whose traversal is narrowed to live lifecycle mutations. `observed-conformance` because insufficiency of proof is established only from post-launch evidence. Added because a launch traversal never reaches L1, so `94` could not bind the launch-failure case its own predicate describes.
entries.traversal: one launch (Create running, Start, or same-Sandbox Restore) traversal, at status publication
entries.remediation: Commit `unknown` with closed admission and retain the launch evidence for a system-originated reconciliation Operation.

entries.title: Teardown seal declared without driver-supplied backend exit and drain evidence
entries.statement: A driver supplies proven backend exit and output-drain evidence for every retained Process stream during Stop or Delete before the Core may seal that stream at teardown.
entries.rationale: Q1: the decision reads the driver's backend-exit observation and its drain evidence for each retained spool on the teardown traversal; both exist only after the teardown effect has acted. Q2: producing and decoding that native evidence is the driver/provider boundary, so runtime owns it; the Core stores the teardown seal but does not observe the backend pipe. Q3: T0 is the teardown station and the last point at which withholding the seal is still correct. Q4: the Core-side teardown obligation to drain, seal, and resolve accepted commands is `191` under a different owner; the exec-outcome half of the driver obligation is `152`, whose traversal is narrowed to one Exec dispatch and its output stream. Observed-conformance because the evidence is provable only after the effect. Added because the locked Stop Completion Protocol assigns the reap-drain-seal step to the portable Stop driver, so the driver obligation does not terminate at E1.
entries.traversal: Sandbox teardown traversal during Stop or Delete, at output drain and seal
entries.remediation: Observe backend exit for every retained Process stream during teardown and drain the transport fully, then supply that evidence so the Core can seal at teardown.
